Author’s Preface
All praises are due to Allāh , the Lord of the universe. May peace and blessings
descend upon our Master, Muḥammad  - the Seal of the Prophets - and upon His
pure family and all His Companions .
The dependant slave of his independent master, Abū al-Ikhlāṣ Ḥasan al-Wafā’i al-
Shurunbulāli, states:
“A few friends - may Allāh  treat us and them with his discreet favours - requested
that I prepare a short treatise on ‘ibādah which abridges for the beginner those masā’il
which are scattered in the voluminous books of Fiq̣h. So I beseeched Allāh  for His
assistance and replied in the affirmative, eager for reward.
I will only mention those masā’il, the authenticity of which has been asserted by the
Ahl at-Tarjīḥ1 without elaboration. I have entitled this treatise ‘Nūr al-Īḍāḥ wa Najāt
al-Arwāḥ’.
I ask Allāh  alone to benefit His servants thereby, and to perpetuate its beneficence.
1 These are those Fuq̣ahāԒ who are entirely dependent on taq̣līd (following the views of higher calibre scholarship).
However, they are able to survey the proofs of a variety of opinions and determine the soundest view and are also able to
arrange the opinions according to their soundness. For example, they may say ‘this opinion is preferred’, ‘this is
sounder’, ‘this is closer to q̣iyāsԒ, etc. These scholars are known as Aṣhāb al-Tarjīḥ. Examples of scholars in this category
include Imam Qudūri  and the author of al-Hidāyah Imam Marghīnāni . (Sharḥ ԑUq̣ūd Rasm al-Muftī, page 24)

text_raw:
The Book of Purity
The types of water with which purity may be attained
These are seven:
1. Rainwater
2. Seawater
3. River water
4. Well water
5. Water from melted snow
6. or hail
7. Spring water
Thereafter, water is classified into five categories:
First Category: pure, purifying and not makrūh (i.e. this type of water is pure in itself,
may be used to purify other things and there is no disapproval in using this kind of
water). And that is general water.
Second Category: pure, purifying and makrūh (i.e. this type of water is pure in itself,
may be used to purify other things. However, it is disliked to use this kind of water.).
This is that water from which a cat or a similar animal has drunk, and that water is less
in quantity.
Third Category: pure and not purifying (i.e. this type of water is pure in itself, but may
not be used to purify other things.), This is that water which has been used to remove
ritual impurity or for attaining reward, such as making wuḍū’ upon another wuḍū’
(i.e. making wuḍū’ whilst in the state of wuḍū’) with the intention of wuḍū’.
The water will become musta‘mal (used) by its mere separation from the body.2
2 This means that the water becomes musta‘mal immediately after separating from the body. Imam Ṭaḥāwi  and some
scholars of Balkh (a provice in Afghanistan) opine that the water only becomes used if it settles in a place and not
immediately after separating from the limb.  (al-Iṣbāḥ ‘alā Nūr al-Īḍāḥ, page 132)
Water with which wuḍū’ is not permitted
Wuḍū’ is not permitted with
a) The water (extracted) from trees and fruits, though it may have come out itself
without squeezing, according to the most apparent view3.
b) The water, the nature of which has changed, due to either cooking or the
overpowering of an external substance.
Overpowering, in the case of a solid substance mixing with the water, will occur due to
the water losing its viscosity (thinness) and fluidity.4 It is not a problem if all the
properties of the water (i.e. taste, colour and smell) change due to a solid substance
such as saffron, fruit and leaves of a tree.
Overpowering, in the case of a fluid mixing with the water, will occur if:
 One property becomes apparent from a liquid which has only two properties.
For example, milk: it has a colour and taste but has no smell5.
 Two properties become apparent from a liquid which has all three properties.
For example, vinegar: it has a colour, taste and smell6.

The Book of Purity
Overpowering in the case of a fluid which has no properties - like used water, and rose
water from which its smell has disappeared – will be ascertained by weight. Thus,
wuḍū’ will not be permissible with water wherein two riṭl of used water were mixed
with one riṭl of pure water. In the opposite scenario, wuḍū’ will be permissible.

made to keep the translation of these terms as consistent as possible. For example, L ѫƊѪįا and ¾:اįѪو have been translated as

Rasm al-Muftī, page 100-102. (Translator)
4 This means that if a solid substance mixes with the water, causing the water to lose its flow and become thick, then this
water will be considered to be overpowered by that substance. (Translator)
5 This means that if water and milk mix and only the taste or only the colour, or both the colour and smell of the milk
become apparent in the water, then this water will be considered to be overpowered and therefore wuḍū’ with such water
will not be permissible. If, however, neither the colour nor the taste become apparent, then wuḍū’ with such water is
correct. (Translator)
6 If any two from amongst these three properties become apparent then wuḍū’ with such water is not permitted.
However, if only one property from the above-mentioned three becomes apparent the water remains unaffected. (ibid.)
Fourth Category: impure water. This is that water into which an impure substance has
fallen, and that water is:
a) Stagnant (not flowing) and less in quantity (less quantity of water is that
amount of water which is less than ten by ten feet). This will become impure
even if the effect of the impure substance does not become apparent in the
water.
b) Flowing and the effect of the impurity becomes apparent in it.
Effects:  Taste, colour or smell.
Fifth Category: doubtful water with regards to its ability to cleanse and purify other

bab: The rulings pertaining to left-over water (Su’r)
text_raw:
The rulings pertaining to left-over water (Su’r)
When a living thing drinks from a small quantity of water it will be classified into four
categories and is given the name ‘su’r’.
First Category: pure and purifying (i.e. this type of water is pure in itself and may be
used to purify other things). This is that water from which a human, horse or an
animal suitable for consumption (i.e. ḥalāl), has drunk.
Second Category: impure water, the usage of which is impermissible. This is that
water from which a dog, pig or an animal of prey e.g. a cheetah or a wolf has drunk.
Third Category: the usage of this water is makrūh with the availability of other water.
This is the left-over water of a cat, free-range chicken, bird of prey e.g. hawk, falcon or
eagle, and household animals such as mice, but not scorpions.
Fourth Category: doubtful water with regards to its ability to cleanse and purify other
things. This is the leftover water of a mule or donkey. If no water besides this is found,
one will perform wuḍū’ with it, perform tayammum (dry ablution) and thereafter
offer his prayer.

text_raw:
Scrutiny (inspection) of utensils and clothing
If many utensils get mixed up, the majority of which are pure, then one will
scrutinise/investigate in order to perform wuḍū’ and to drink therefrom. If the
majority of the utensils are impure, then one will not scrutinise, except for drinking.
(As for wuḍū’, he will perform tayammum instead, as if he has no water.)
In the case of mixed clothing, one will investigate, regardless whether the majority are
pure or impure.7

bab: Rulings pertaining to the purifying of wells
text_raw:
Rulings pertaining to the purifying of wells
A small well
1) This will be (completely) emptied
 Due to the falling of an impurity (though it may be little), besides manure. E.g.
a drop of blood or alcohol
 Due to the falling of a pig, though it may have exited the well alive, without its
mouth having touched the water8.
 Due to the death of a dog9, sheep or human within the well.
 Due to the bloating of an animal, though it may be small.
2) Two hundred buckets (of water) will be removed if the emptying of the entire well
is impossible.
3) If a chicken, cat or a similar animal dies inside the well it will be necessary to
remove forty buckets of water.
4) If a mouse or a similar animal dies inside the well it will be necessary to remove
twenty buckets of water.
This will be cleansing for:
1) The well
2) Bucket
3) Rope
4) Hand of the person who is removing the water
Those things which do not make the well impure
7 This is because water has a replacement in the form of pure soil etc. by which he can make tayammum, whereas
clothing has no replacement. (al-Iṣbāḥ, page 135)
8 The entire pig is impure. Therefore the well will become impure due to it falling inside it. (ibid.)
9 The dog will render the water impure by dying within the well, not by merely falling inside (provided its mouth and
saliva have not touched the water) because the dog is not totally impure, contrary to the pig. (al-Iṣbāḥ, page 136)
The well will not become impure due to
1) The excretion of camels and sheep/goats
2) The excretion of horses, donkeys and mules
3) The manure of cattle
except
1) If it appears to be in excessive amounts to the observer
2) Or if not a single bucket is empty from the excretion
Those things which do not contaminate the well
The well will not become contaminated due to
1) The excretion of pigeons and sparrows.
2) Nor due to the death of such an animal in which there is no blood. For
example, fish, frogs, all aquatic animals (animals which live in water), fleas,
flies, wasps and scorpions.
3) Nor due to the falling of a human being or animal suitable for consumption
provided that the person (or animal) exit alive and there was no impurity upon
his body.
4) Nor due to the falling of a mule, donkey, bird of prey or wild animal according
to the sound position.
If the saliva of the fallen (person or animal) reaches the water it will adopt its (the
saliva’s) ruling.
The presence of a dead animal within the well will render the well to have been impure

text_raw:
Rules pertaining to istinjā’
Istibrā’ is necessary for a male until the effects of urine are removed and his heart is
content, according to his usual practice: either by
a) Walking     b) Coughing     c) Lying down
Or, by any other method which leaves him content.
It is not permissible for him to start performing wuḍū’ until he is content that the
drops of urine have indeed stopped.
The ruling of istinjā’
To perform istinjā’ from every type of impurity which is excreted from the two paths
is sunnah, so long as the impurity does not exceed the place of exit.
However, if the excreted impurity does surpass (the place of exit) and is equivalent to a
dirham, then its removal with water becomes wājib.
If it exceeds a dirham then to wash it away becomes farḍ.
It is farḍ to wash the impurity which is within the place of exit whilst bathing (to
achieve purity) from janābah, ḥaiḍ and nifās, though that impurity may be little.
(It is also sunnah) to perform istinjā’ with stones capable of cleansing, or something
similar, whilst to cleanse with water is more preferred. However, the combined use of
water and stones is most desirable. First, the individual will wipe (using the stones
etc.), and thereafter wash (using the water.)
It is permissible to suffice upon the usage of stones or water alone.
To cleanse the area is sunnah, whilst the quantity of stones to be used is merely
mustaḥab, not an emphasised sunnah (sunnah al-mu’akkadah). Therefore, istinjā’ will
be performed with three stones, though cleanliness may be achieved with fewer stones;
hence, it is mustaḥab.
The manner of performing istinjā’
The manner of performing istinjā’ is as follows:
A male will wipe with the first stone (of the three), from the front side towards the
back, then from the back side towards the front with the second stone and lastly, from
the front side towards the back with the third, if the scrotum is dangling.
If the scrotum, however, is not dangling, the male will start from the back side,
(wiping) towards the front.
A female will in all circumstances begin from the front side, (wiping) towards the back
for fear of dirtying her genitalia.
Thereafter, the individual will first wash his hands and then proceed to scrub the area
with the palm-side of one, two or even three fingers if necessary. In the initial stages of
Istinjā’, the individual will raise his middle finger above the rest, and then his ring
finger. He will not suffice upon the usage of a single finger.

Rules pertaining to istinjā’
A female will raise her ring finger and her middle finger from the beginning, for fear of
getting pleasure.
The individual will go to a great length in cleaning until the foul odour remains no
more, and in loosening the rear orifice, provided that he is not fasting.
Once finished, he will wash his hands for the second time and dry his rear prior to
standing, if fasting.

bab: The etiquettes and disliked actions of istinjā’
text_raw:
The etiquettes and disliked actions of istinjā’
It is not permissible to expose ones ‘awrah in order to perform istinjā’ (in the presence
of another who can see him.)
If the impurity exceeds its place of exit and the exceeding impurity is more than a
dirham, then ṣalāh with such impurity will not be correct if such an item is available
with which he can remove it.
One will make istinjā’ discreetly (without exposing the ‘awrah) in the presence of one
who may see him.
Items with which istinjā’ is makrūh
Istinjā’ is makrūh with:
a) Bones
b) Food of human beings or animals
c) Bricks
d) Wet mud/clay
e) Coal
f) Glass
g) Limestone
h) A sanctified item e.g. a piece of silk or cotton
i) And with the right hand, except due to an excuse
Etiquettes of fulfilling the call of nature
One will enter the toilet with his left foot, seeking refuge in Allāh  from the accursed
devil prior to entering, and sit leaning upon his left side. The individual will not speak
except out of necessity.
It is makrūh taḥrīmi:
a) To face the Q̣iblah and to turn one back towards it, even within the confines of
an enclosure.
b) To directly face the sun, moon or the direction of the wind.
It is makrūh to urinate or excrete:
a) In water
b) A shade
c) A hole/burrow
d) Upon a road
e) Under a fruitful tree
f) (urinate) standing except due to an excuse
One will exit the toilet with his right foot, and then recite:

text_raw:
Rules pertaining to wuḍū’
The requisites of wuḍū’ are four, and they are its farā’iḍ:
1) The washing of the face;
Its boundary, lengthwise: from the raised portion of the upper forehead until the
bottom of the chin.
Its boundary, breadthwise: the entire area between the two earlobes.
2) Washing of both hands including both elbows
3) Washing of both feet including both ankles
4) Masaḥ of a quarter of the head
The reason for (performing) wuḍū’: to sanction (make permissible) all such acts
which are impermissible without it (i.e. wuḍū’). This is the worldly ruling. As for the
ruling of the hereafter, (the reason for performing wuḍū’ is) to attain reward in the
Ākhirah.
Conditions for rendering wuḍū’ wājib:
1) Intellect     2) Puberty     3) To be Muslim    4) To be capable of using sufficient
water          5) The existence of ḥadath     6&7) Absence of ḥaiḍ and nifās     8) Lack of
time (excluding janāzah and the two Eid prayers)
The conditions for wuḍū’ to be correct are three:
1) To encompass the skin with purifying water,
2) The discontinuing of those things which disallow (an individual to perform) wuḍū’
i.e. ḥaiḍ, nifās and ḥadath,
3) To remove all such things which prevent the water from reaching the skin e.g. wax
and fat.

Rulings pertaining to wuḍū’
It is incumbent to wash the external portion of a thick beard according to the most
correct position upon which the fatwa is given. It is compulsory to make the water
reach the skin underlying a thin beard.
It is not necessary to make the water reach the tips of those hairs which are exposed
from the circumference of the face, nor to that portion of the lips which becomes
concealed when the mouth is closed.
If the fingers are webbed, or the finger-nails become so long that they conceal the
fingertips, or there is such a thing within the finger-nails which prevents water (from
penetrating), e.g. kneaded dough, then to wash the portion under the finger-nails
becomes necessary.
Dirt, the excretion of fleas and the like do not prevent the (penetration) of water.
To rotate a constricted (tight) ring is also necessary.
If washing the cracks upon his feet harms him, it is permissible for an individual to
pass water over the ointment which he has applied to them.
Neither masaḥ nor washing will be repeated upon the place of hair after shaving it.
Washing will not be repeated due to clipping the nails or trimming the moustache.

text_raw:
Types of wuḍū’
Wuḍū’ is of three types:
First: farḍ upon the individual who is in the state of ḥadath (ritual impurity) so that he
may:
a) Offer ṣalāh, though it may be nafl
b) Offer the funeral prayers
c) Make sajdat al-tilāwah (prostration of recitation)
d) Touch the Q̣ur’ān, even if it be a single verse
Second: wājib, in order to perform ṭawāf of the Ka‘bah.
Third: mandūb (preferable)
a) To sleep in the state of ablution
b)To wake up in the state of ablution
c) To remain constantly in the state of wuḍū’
d) To perform wuḍū’ upon an existing wuḍū’
e) After backbiting, lying and tale-bearing
f) After every sin
g) After reciting licentious (dirty) poetry
h) After laughing aloud outside ṣalāh
i) After bathing and lifting a deceased person
j) For every prayer time
k) Prior to bathing due to janābah
l) For the person in the state of janābah when intending to eat, drink, sleep or copulate
again
m) When in the state of anger
n) To recite Q̣ur’ān
o) To recite and narrate hadith
p) To participate in a gathering of religious learning
q) To call the adhān, iq̣āmah or give the khuṭbah
r) To visit the grave of the Prophet 
s) To stop over at ‘Arafah and to perform sa’y between Mount Ṣafa and Marwah
t) After eating camel meat
u) In order to exclude oneself from the differences of opinion amongst the scholars,
for instance after touching a woman

text_raw:
Those things which nullify wuḍū’
Twelve things will nullify wuḍū’:
1) All substances which are excreted from the two paths besides the air which is
emitted from the front, according to the soundest view.
2) A child-birth without the witnessing of blood
3) Flowing impurity from any another part of the body besides the two paths e.g.
blood and pus
4) Vomiting up food, water, clotted blood or bile, if it fills the mouth
Criteria for a full mouth: if the mouth cannot be closed upon it except with difficulty,
according to the soundest view.
Different bouts of vomit will be considered as one if the cause is one and the same.
5) Blood which has overwhelmed the saliva or has equalled it
6) Sleeping in such a manner that the buttocks are not firmly placed on the ground
7) The raising of the buttocks of a sleeping person prior to waking up, even if he
doesn’t fall, according to the ẓāhir al-riwāyah
8) Fainting
9) Madness
10) Intoxication
11) The loud laughing of a mature person, whilst awake, in a prayer consisting of
rukū’ and sajdah, though the individual may have intended to abort his prayer thereby
12) To touch the female genitalia part with an erect male genitalia without any barrier

text_raw:
Things which necessitate ghusl
Ghusl becomes incumbent (farḍ) due to one of the following seven things:
1) The ejaculating of semen out of the body when it separates from its place of storage
with pleasure, without sexual intercourse
2) The disappearing of the head of the male genitalia - or an equivalent length in the
case when it has been cut - in any of the two paths of a living human being
3) Ejaculation due to copulating with a corpse or an animal
4) The presence of a thin liquid substance after sleep provided his genitalia was not
erect prior to going sleep
5) The presence of wetness which he considers to be semen after coming to his senses
from intoxication or after fainting
6&7) Menstrual periods and post-natal bleeding
Even if the aforementioned causes occur prior to accepting Islam, it will still be
incumbent to perform ghusl according to the soundest view.
The bathing of a deceased individual is farḍ al-kifāyah.

text_raw:
The sunan of ghusl
Twelve actions are sunnah in ghusl:
1) To begin with Bismillāh,
2) To make the intention,
3) To wash both hands till the wrists,
4) To wash all impurities, even if separately (i.e. prior to commencing ghusl),
5) To wash the genitals
6) And thereafter the individual will perform wuḍū’ as he does for ṣalāh. Therefore, he
will wash each limb thrice and make masaḥ of the head. However, he will delay the
washing of both feet if standing in such a place wherein water gathers.
7) Thereafter he will pour water upon his body thrice. If an individual were to dive
into flowing water, or that which holds the same ruling, and remain therein for a
while, then verily he would have completed the sunnah
8) He will start with pouring the water on his head
9) Thereafter he will wash his right shoulder
10) Then his left shoulder
11) He will scrub his body
12) And will keep the washing perpetual (continuous, without pause).

Ghusl is sunnah on four occasions:

2) The prayers of the two Eids

4&5) after cupping and bathing a corpse,

10) In order to enter Makkah,
11) In order to perform the ṭawāf al-ziyārah
12&16) and for the prayers performed at the time of:
a) A Solar eclipse     b) Drought     c) Intense fear     d) Enveloping darkness (during the
day)     e) Gale-force winds

text_raw:
Tayammum
Tayammum is correct with the following eight conditions:
1) Intention;
The essence of intention: to make a firm resolve in the heart of carrying out a certain
action.
The time for making intention: when striking the hands upon the item with which he
is making tayammum.
There are three conditions in order for the intention to be correct:
1) To be Muslim     2) To possess a sound intellect     3) and to know that action which
he is making the intention for.
One of three things are conditional in order for the intention of tayammum to be
correct and thereby offer ṣalāh:
1) The intention of attaining purity,
2) The intention to make ṣalāh permissible (for himself)
3) The intention of a certain act of devotion (al-‘ibādah al-maq̣sūdah: an act of
worship which has not become necessary due to an external factor. Rather, from the
onset, it is an ordained act of devotion whereby closeness to Allāh is achieved) which
will not be correct without purity.
Therefore, an individual may not perform ṣalāh if he has merely made the intention of
tayammum, or has made the intention of reciting the Q̣ur’ān whilst not in the state of
janābah.
2) An excuse which permits tayammum for example:
a) Being a mile’s distance from water, even if in a city
b) The presence of an illness or severe cold due to which there is a fear of perishing or
illness
c) The fear of an enemy or thirst
d) The need of water in order to knead dough, not for the preparation of a stew
e) The lack of apparatuses (tools required for extracting the water from its source)
f) The fear of missing janāzah and ‘Īd prayers, even if on the basis of binā’
The fear of missing the Jumu‘ah and farḍ prayers is not considered a sufficient excuse.
3) That tayammum be performed with a pure substance from the genus of the earth.
For example soil, rock and sand, not wood, silver or gold.
4) To encompass the entire surface area with the masaḥ.
5) To make masaḥ with the entire hand, or with most of it. Hence, if an individual
makes masaḥ with two fingers only, it will not be sufficient and permissible, even if he
repeatedly makes masaḥ (with these two fingers) until he covers the entire surface
area, contrary to the masaḥ of the head.
6) That tayammum be performed with two strikes of both palms, even if upon one
place.
Dust blowing onto the body is equivalent to striking (the earth etc.) twice if masaḥ is
made using this dust with the intention of tayammum.

text_raw:
Tayammum
7) The ceasing of those things which prevent tayammum i.e. ḥaiḍ, nifās and ḥadath.
8) The removal of all substances (from the surface of the skin) which prevent masaḥ,
for example, wax and fat.
The cause and conditions for tayammum are the same as those mentioned in wuḍū’.
The two components of tayammum are: 1) to make masaḥ of both hands and 2) the
face.
There are seven sunan of tayammum:
1) To recite Bismillāh at the beginning
2) To follow the prescribed sequence
3) To ensure the masaḥ is perpetual (continuous, without pause)
4) To move both hands forwards after placing them on the soil
5) Then to draw them back
6) To dust the hands
7) To keep the fingers spaced apart
It is preferable to delay tayammum for an individual who has hopes of attaining water
prior to the time finishing.
It is wājib to delay the ṣalāh upon the promise of water even if there is a fear of missing
the prescribed time.
It is wājib to delay ṣalāh upon the promise of clothing or apparatus (for extracting
water from its source) so long as there is no fear of missing the prescribed time.
It is wājib to search for water for the distance of four hundred steps if he considers it to
be close with safety, or else it is not wājib.
It is likewise wājib to make enquiries (about water) from the one who is accompanying
him if in such an area where people are not miserly with (i.e. are not rationing) water
supplies. If the companion does not give him the water except in exchange for its
average price (thaman al-mithl) then to buy it will become necessary upon him, if he
has with him finances in excess of his expenditure.
An individual may pray as many farā’iḍ and nawāfil as he likes, with a single
tayammum. It is correct to perform tayammum prior to the time (of ṣalāh) setting in.
If a major portion or half of the body is injured, then tayammum will be made. If,
however, most of the body is sound, then he will wash (the sound part) and make
masaḥ of the injured area. One may not combine washing and tayammum together.
The very same things which break wuḍū’ will also break tayammum. In addition, the
capability to use sufficient water (will also nullify tayammum.)
If an individual missing both hands and feet has a facial injury, he will offer ṣalāh
without any form of purification and will not repeat the prayer.

text_raw:
Masaḥ upon the socks
It is correct to make masaḥ upon both socks in the case of lesser impurity (ḥadath al-
aṣghar) for both men and women, even if the socks are made of any other thick
material besides leather, regardless of whether the sole is made of leather or not.
Seven prerequisites are conditional for permission to make masaḥ upon the socks:
1) To wear both socks after washing both feet, even if prior to the completion of
wuḍū’, provided that the wuḍū’ is completed before the occurrence of anything which
nullifies wuḍū’.
2) Both socks must cover the ankles.
3) The possibility of walking in them continuously. Therefore, it will not be
permissible to make masaḥ upon a sock made from glass, wood or metal.
4) Both socks have to be free from tears (rips) equivalent to three fingers: each finger
being the size of the smallest toe.
5) Both must be secured to the feet without tying.
6) Both must prevent water from reaching the body surface (i.e. Must be water-proof).
7) It is also a condition that the equivalent of three fingers of the hand remains from
the front part of the foot. Therefore, an individual missing the front part of his foot
will not be permitted to make masaḥ, even if the heel-side of his foot remains.
The duration of masaḥ
A muq̣īm (resident) may continue to make masaḥ for a full day and night (24 hours)
and a musāfir (traveller) for three consecutive days and nights (72 hours).
The duration (of 24 hours) commences when the wuḍū’ breaks (ḥadath) after wearing
the socks.
If a muq̣īm makes masaḥ and thereafter travels prior to the completion of the duration
then he will complete the duration of a traveller (72 hours).
If a traveller becomes a muq̣īm after already having made masaḥ for a day and night
(24 hours) he will remove the sock. If he has not (completed 24 hours), then he will be
able to complete (i.e. continue to make masaḥ) for a day and night.
The farḍ of masaḥ
The minimal area for masaḥ is three fingers – each being the size of the smallest finger
- upon the upper front portion of both feet.
The sunan of masaḥ
To stretch the fingers, whilst keeping them apart, from the tips of the toes until the
shins.
Those things which nullify the masaḥ upon the socks
These are four:
1) Everything which breaks wuḍū’
2) The removal of the sock, even if (the full sock has not been removed but the sock
has slid down to such an extent that) a major portion of the foot has come into the
shin-part of the sock.

bab: Rules pertaining to bandages and the like
text_raw:
Rules pertaining to bandages and the like
If a person has been cupped, injured or has broken a limb, and thereafter has fastened
it with a sling or bandage and is therefore unable to wash the limb, nor can he make
masaḥ upon it, then it is wājib upon him to make masaḥ upon a majority portion of
that (bandage etc.) which he has used to fasten the limb.
It will be sufficient to make masaḥ upon the portion of the limb which is visible
through the bandage of one who has been cupped.
Masaḥ is like ghusl. Therefore it is not restricted to a specific duration.
It is not a condition that the bandage is worn whilst in the state of purity.
Furthermore, it is permissible to make masaḥ on the bandaged foot whilst washing the
other (which is not bandaged).
The masaḥ is not nullified if the bandage comes off prior to the wound healing.
It is permissible to replace the bandage with another. It will not be necessary to repeat
the masaḥ upon the new bandage. However, it is better to remake masaḥ.
If an individual
 Suffers from an eye infection and is ordered not to apply water to his eyes
 Or has broken a nail and has applied an ointment or balm to it, and its removal
may prove harmful to him
then it is permissible for him to make masaḥ. However, if masaḥ is also harmful to
him, then he may leave masaḥ altogether.
An intention is not necessary in order to make masaḥ on the socks, a bandage or the
head.

bab: Ḥaiḍ, Nifās and Istiḥāḍah (Menstruation, Post-natal Bleeding and Chronic Vaginal Discharge)
text_raw:
Ḥaiḍ, Nifās and Istiḥāḍah (Menstruation, Post-natal Bleeding and Chronic
Vaginal Discharge)
The following are discharged from the female genitalia:
1. Ḥaiḍ (menstruation)
2. Nifās (post-natal bleeding)
3. Istiḥāḍah (chronic vaginal discharge)
Ḥaiḍ: is that blood which is discharged from the womb of a female who has reached
the age of puberty provided she has no illness, is not pregnant and has not reached the
age of menopause.
The minimum duration of ḥaiḍ (menstruation) is three days, whilst the average is five
days and the maximum is ten days.
Nifās: is that blood which is discharged after childbirth. The maximum duration of
Nifās is forty days while there is no restriction upon the minimum duration.
Istiḥāḍah: is that blood which is discharged for less than three days or more than ten
days in the menstrual cycle, or more than forty days in post-natal bleeding.
The minimum duration of purity separating two menstruations is fifteen days. There
is no limit to the maximum duration except for a female who attained puberty in the
state of istiḥāḍah.
Eight things become impermissible due to menstruation and post-natal bleeding:
1) Offering ṣalāh,
2) Fasting,
3) Reciting a verse from the Qur’an,
4) To touch the Qur’an except with a cover
5) To enter the masjid
6) To make ṭawāf
7) To have sexual intercourse
8) To take pleasure from beneath the navel to beneath the knees
If the blood has stopped flowing upon the completion of the maximum duration for
ḥaiḍ and nifās, then it is permissible to have intercourse prior to bathing.
However, it will not be permissible to have intercourse if the blood has stopped prior
to the completion of the maximum duration due to the normal habit of this particular
female unless:
1) She bathes
2) Or makes tayammum and performs a ṣalāh
3) Or if a prayer becomes a debt upon her (i.e. becomes q̣aḍā’)
Ṣalāh will become a debt upon her if she finds sufficient time (within the prayer time
in which the blood stopped) to perform ghusl and taḥrīmah (to initiate ṣalāh) after the
blood has stopped, but this female does not bathe nor does she perform tayammum
until the time (for that prayer) finishes.
A menstruating female and a female who is the state of nifās (post-natal bleeding) will
make up (do q̣aḍā’) of the missed fasts not the missed prayers.
Being in the state of janābah will make the following five things impermissible:
1) To perform ṣalāh
2) To read any verse from the Qur’an
3) To touch the Qur’an except with a cover

4) To enter the masjid
5) To perform ṭawāf
Three things are impermissible for an individual in the state of ḥadath (i.e. a person
who is not in the state of wuḍū’):
1) To perform ṣalāh
2) To perform ṭawāf
3) To touch the Qur’an except with a cover
The blood of istiḥāḍah (chronic vaginal discharge) holds the same ruling as a constant
nosebleed:
It will not prevent ṣalāh, fasting or sexual intercourse.
A female suffering from istiḥāḍah (chronic vaginal discharge) and every other
individual who suffers from a chronic ailment (e.g. incontinence of the bowel
[inability to control urine] and chronic release of wind) will perform wuḍū’ at every
prayer time. Thereafter, they will be able to perform as many farā’iḍ and nawāfil as
they wish (within that certain prayer time).
The wuḍū’ of one suffering from a chronic condition will be nullified by the
termination of that prayer time only.
When the individual will become ma’dhūr
The individual will not be considered ma’dhūr (excused) until the excuse remains for
the full duration of a prayer time without a cessation (break) in which wuḍū’ and ṣalāh
can be performed. This is the criteria for classifying an individual as ma’dhūr
(excused).
The condition for this ruling to remain is the excuse must be found in following
prayer times, even if once. (I.e. in order for the individual to continue being
considered ma’dhūr, the excuse must be found in following prayer times at least
once.)
When the individual will cease to be ma’dhūr
If one full time for prayer passes without the excuse being found therein, the
individual’s excuse will no longer be valid and he will cease to be considered ma’dhūr.

Impurities and cleansing them
Najāsat is categorized into two types:
1) Ghalīẓah (dense/heavy type)
2) Khafīfah (light type)
Ghalīẓah: For example; wine, flowing blood, flesh and skin of carrion, the urine of
such an animal which is impermissible to eat, the excretion of dogs and animals of
prey, their saliva, the excretion of chickens, ducks and geese, and all those things
which nullify wuḍū’ due to coming out the body of an individual.
Khafīfah: For example, the urine of horses and all those animals which are permissible
for consumption and the excretion of such birds which cannot be eaten.
Najāsat al-ghalīẓah equivalent to the size (or weight) of a dirham is excused. Similarly
,najāsat al-khafīfah equivalent to a quarter of one’s clothing or limb is excused.
Sprinkles of urine equivalent to the tip of a needle are also excused.
If impure soil or an impure bed becomes wet due to the perspiration (sweat) of a
sleeping person or due to the wetness of the feet and the effect of the impurity
becomes apparent upon the body or foot, they will both become impure. If, however,
the impurity does not visualise (become apparent), they will remain pure.
Similarly, that pure dry piece of clothing which has been wrapped in an impure damp
piece of clothing which cannot be squeezed when wrung, will not become impure.
A damp piece of clothing will not become impure due to spreading it out on dry
impure land which becomes wet due to it (i.e. due to the damp piece of cloth).
Similarly, a piece of clothing will not become impure due to the wind which blows
upon an impurity and thereafter reaches the piece of clothing except, of course, if the
effect of the impurity becomes apparent on the piece of clothing.
A visible impurity becomes pure by merely removing it, even if (this is achieved) by
washing it once according to the sound position. The lingering of an effect which is
difficult to remove is not a problem. An invisible impurity becomes pure by washing
the item thrice and squeezing it every time.
An impurity may be removed from clothing and the body by water and every
purifying liquid. For example, vinegar and rose water. Leather socks and the like may
be purified by merely rubbing an impurity which has a (visible) form even if it is wet.
Swords and the like will become pure by wiping them down.

text_raw:
Purifying leather and the like
The skin of a dead animal will become pure by:
a) Actual tanning (al-dibāghah al-haq̣īqiyyah) for example, using leaves of an acacia
(nilotica) tree
b) Partial tanning (al-dibāghah al-ḥukmiyyah) for example, smothering it in soil or
sun-drying it
This is the case with all animal skins besides the skin of a pig or a human being. (These
two will remain impure even after tanning.)
Slaughtering according to the shar‘ī method will purify (only) the skin of those
animals which are impermissible to consume, not the flesh according to the most
correct position upon which the fatwa is given.
All those body parts in which blood does not flow will not become impure due to
death. For example, hair, a plucked feather, horns, hooves and bones provided they are
not covered in fat. Tendons/nerves are impure according to the sound position.
The pouch in which the musk is stored is pure as is the musk itself and its
consumption is permissible. The musk produced by the civet cat is also pure; the ṣalāh
of an individual who has applied it will be correct.

text_raw:
The Book of Ṣalāh
Three things are conditional in order for ṣalāh to become farḍ:
1. To be Muslim     2. To be bāligh     3. To be of sound intellect
Children of seven years of age will be instructed to offer ṣalāh and children of ten years
will be beaten by hand (not using a stick) due to missing it.
The cause (sabab) of ṣalāh
The cause of every prayer is (the entry of) the prescribed timings. Ṣalāh becomes
compulsory (immediately) at the beginning of the prescribed time though the
compulsion is extended (wujūb muwassa‘a).
There are five prescribed timings:
1. The time of the Morning Prayer (Fajr) starts with the appearance of true dawn
till shortly before sunrise.
2. The time of the Ẓuhr prayer starts from zawāl (when the sun moves slightly
from the meridian) till the shadow of everything becomes
a. Double (in size)
b. Or the same size (as the actual item)
excluding ẓill al-istiwā’ (the original shadow which is present at noon).
Imam Ṭaḥāwi  has given preference to the second statement, which is the position
of the Ṣāḥibayn .
3. The time of ‘Aṣr begins from when the shadow begins to extend further than
double or the same size (as the actual item) till the setting of the sun.
4. Maghrib begins from then (i.e. sunset) till when the al-shafaq̣ al-aḥmar
(redness in the sky) fades, according to the opinion upon which the fatwa is
given.
5. ‘Ishā’ and Witr begin from here (i.e. the end time of Maghrib) till true dawn.
Witr will not be offered prior to ‘Ishā’ due to the order being compulsory.
Whoever does not find the time for ‘Ishā and Witr, (i.e. the time for ‘Ishā and Witr
does not start at all in that certain place) they will not be compulsory upon him.
Two farḍs may not be combined in a single prescribed timing due to any reason,
except in the plains of ‘Arafah for a haji with the conditions of (the presence) of the
Imam al-A‘ẓam (the caliph or his deputy) and iḥrām. Only then will jam‘ taq̣dīm
(advanced combining) be permissible between Ẓuhr and ‘Aṣr (i.e. both will be
performed in the time of Ẓuhr) and (jam‘ ta’khīr [delayed combining] between)
Maghrib and ‘Ishā’ in Muzdalifah. It is not permissible to perform Maghrib on the
road to Muzdalifah.
Mustaḥab prayer times
It is mustaḥab
 To delay the Fajr prayer till it becomes fairly light (for men)
 To pray Ẓuhr in the cool period in the summer season
 To offer Ẓuhr early in the winter season except on a cloudy and overcast day
wherein it will be delayed

bab: Times in which ṣalāh is impermissible and times in which ṣalāh is makrūh
text_raw:
Times in which ṣalāh is impermissible and times in which ṣalāh is makrūh
Three times are such that it is impermissible to perform such a farḍ or wājib which
became a debt upon him (i.e. q̣aḍā’) prior to the entry of these three times:
1) Whilst the sun is rising until it has fully risen
2) When the sun reaches the meridian (zawāl) until it moves slightly
3) Once the sun becomes pale yellow until it sets
It is permissible to offer any prayer which becomes incumbent upon an individual
within these times. For example,
a) A funeral which has appeared
b) The sajdah for an ayah which has been recited in one of these three times
c) It will be valid (though disliked) to offer that day’s ‘Aṣr prayer whilst the sun is
setting.
It is makrūh at-taḥrīmi to offer nafl ṣalāh in the above-mentioned three times, even if
there is a reason for praying them. For example if a person has sworn to offer nafl
prayers or the two rakā‘ah of ṭawāf.

bab: The times in which it is makrūh to offer nafl prayers
text_raw:
The times in which it is makrūh to offer nafl prayers
It is makrūh to offer nafl ṣalāh
 After al-subḥ al-ṣādiq̣ in excess of the two sunnah of Fajr
 After Fajr ṣalāh
 After ‘Aṣr ṣalāh
 Before Maghrib ṣalāh begins
 Once the khaṭīb appears until he finishes the ṣalāh
 Whilst the iq̣āmah is being called, except the two sunnah of Fajr
 Before the Eid prayer - even at home
 After the Eid prayer in the masjid
 Between the combined prayers in ‘Arafah and Muzdalifah
 When there is a lack of time to offer the farḍ prayer
 Whilst supressing the urge to urinate or excrete
 In the presence of food which one desires
 In the presence of something which is a cause of distraction and affects his
concentration and devotion

Makrūhāt
It is undesirable to (call out adhān) in a singing tone.
The adhān and iq̣āmah of an individual who is in the state of ḥadath is also disliked.

bab: The prerequisites of ṣalāh and its components
text_raw:
The prerequisites of ṣalāh and its components
Twenty seven things are necessary in order for ṣalāh to be correct:
1) To be pure from ḥadath and that the body, clothing and place are pure from an
inexcusable (amount of) impurity, including the place of the feet, hands, knees and
forehead, according to the soundest view.
2) To cover the ‘awrah. It is not a problem if the ‘awrah is visible from the collar-slit
or from beneath the hem of the clothing.
3) To face the q̣iblah. For a person who is in the blessed city of Makkah who can see
the Ka‘bah it is incumbent to pray directly towards it. As for a person who cannot
see the Ka‘bah it is necessary for him to pray in its direction, even if in Makkah,
according to the sound position.
4) The (correct) time
5) To be certain that the time has entered
6) To make an intention
7) To make taḥrīmah without an interruption
8) To make taḥrīmah whilst standing before bending for rukū‘
9) To not delay the intention till after the takbīr of taḥrīmah
10) To verbally utter the takbīr of taḥrīmah in such a manner that he himself can hear
it according to the soundest view.
11) To make the intention of following for the one praying behind an Imam (muq̣tadī)
12) To specify the farḍ prayers (in the intention)
13) And to specify the wājib prayers (in the intention). It is not conditional to make a
specific intention in nafl prayers.
14) To stand in all prayers besides nafl ṣalāh
15) To recite - even if a single verse - in two rakā‘ah of farḍ prayers and in every
rakā’ah of nafl and Witr prayers. No portion of the Q̣ur’ān has been specified in
order for the ṣalāh to be correct. The muq̣tadī will not read. Rather he will listen
attentively and remain silent. If he reads, it is makrūh taḥrīmi.
16) To make rukū‘
17) To make sajdah upon such a surface which he can feel and upon which his
forehead settles, albeit upon his palms or part of his clothing, provided that the
place is pure. It is necessary to make sajdah with the hard bone of the nose and the
forehead. It is not correct to suffice upon the nose unless there is something wrong
with the forehead.
18) The place of sujūd should not be more than half dhirā‘12 above the place of
standing. If the place of sujūd is more than half a dhirā‘ above the place of
standing, sajdah upon such a place is impermissible unless, if due to crowd density,
an individual makes sujūd upon the back of another individual who is offering the
same ṣalāh as him.

bab: The prerequisites of ṣalāh and its components
text_raw:
The prerequisites of ṣalāh and its components
19) To place both hands and both knees, according to the sound position.
20) To place a few toes of both feet on the ground whilst in prostration. It is not
sufficient to merely place the laces of both feet upon the ground.
21) To perform rukū‘ prior to sujūd
22) To rise from sujūd until close to the sitting posture according to the soundest view
23) To return to the second sajdah
24) To sit in q̣ā‘idah al-akhīrah for the duration of tashahhud
25) To delay it (i.e. the q̣āԒidah al-akhīrah) till after all the other arkān
26) To carry out all the arkān whilst awake
27) To be aware of the feature of the prayer (i.e. this prayer is farḍ or this prayer is
sunnah), or to be certain that the ṣalāh that he is offering is farḍ, lest he makes the
intention of offering nafl in farḍ ṣalāh
Arkān of ṣalāh
Four from the above-mentioned twenty seven are arkān:
1) To stand
2) To recite
3) To make rukū‘
4) To make sujūd
Q̣ā’idah al-akhīrah for the duration of tashahhud is also said to be from amongst the
arkān.
12 The dhirā‘ was an ancient measurement used by the Arabs. Originally, two types of dhirā‘ were common; one used to
measure distance (of roads, et al.) and another used to measure clothing. Although there is a difference of opinion as to
which type of dhirā‘ is usually referred to in books of Jurisprudence, the correct view is the dhirā‘ used to measure
clothing, which in juristic terminology is known as ‘dhirā‘ kirbās’. The length of one dhirā‘ kirbās is 18 inches or 45.72
centimetres. (Jawāhir al-Fiq̣h, vol. 3 – summarised, pages 419-421)
The conditions of ṣalāh
The remaining (twenty three) are conditions. Some are conditional in order for the
commencement of ṣalāh to be correct (these are those conditions which are outside of
ṣalāh) whilst others are conditional in to ensure that the ṣalāh remains correct.

text_raw:
Related masā’il
It is permissible to pray
 Upon a saddle-cloth, the upper side of which is pure and the lower-side is impure.
 Upon a pure piece of cloth, the inner lining of which is impure, provided they are
not sewn together.
 Upon the pure part (of a partly impure carpet, mat or cloth), even if the impure
part moves with his movements, according to the sound position.
If one of the two tails of his turban becomes impure and the individual thus allows it to
dangle, whilst keeping the pure tail upon his head in such a manner that the impure
portion does not move with his movements, then his ṣalāh will be valid. If, however,
the impure portion does move, then the person’s prayer will be invalid.
An individual who cannot find anything to remove impurity (from his body or
clothing) will pray with the impurity and will not have to repeat it.
Similarly, an individual who cannot find anything, not even silk, grass or mud, to
cover his ‘awrah, will not have to repeat his prayer.
If he finds something, even if someone has only temporarily allowed him to use it, and
one quarter of it is pure, then to pray unclothed will be incorrect. However, if less than
one quarter is pure than he has been given a choice (between using it and not using it).
Nevertheless, to pray in a totally impure garment is better than praying unclothed.
If he finds something with which he can cover a part of his ‘awrah then it will
incumbent upon him to use it. He will cover his font and back private parts. If it is

prayer. If, however, it is not equivalent to a quarter then it will not prevent the
correctness of the ṣalāh.
Whoever is unable to face the q̣iblah due to illness, or is unable to dismount from his
conveyance, or fears an enemy, his q̣iblah will be whichever direction is possible and
safe.
If the direction of the q̣iblah becomes indiscernible (he does not know the direction of
the q̣iblah), and there is no informant nor any alcove (miḥrāb), the individual will
make taḥarrī (a rational assumption based on existing evidences after a great deal of
thought). If he errs, he will not have to repeat his ṣalāh.
If he becomes aware of his misjudgement in his prayer he will turn towards the correct
direction and continue with his prayer.
If the individual had started his ṣalāh without taḥarrī and upon completion finds out
that he had prayed in the correct direction, his prayer will be valid.
However, if he finds out that he is praying in the right direction during his prayer then
his ṣalāh will become invalid. Similarly, if he did not know the correct direction of the
q̣iblah from the onset (thus, he had started is prayer in uncertainty), his prayer will be
invalid.
If a group of people, according to their rational judgements, pray in many different
directions and are unaware of the situation of the Imam (they do not know his
direction), their prayer will be valid.

The wājibāt of ṣalāh:
There are eighteen wājibāt:
1) To recite al-Fātiḥah
2) To join another sūrah or three verses in two unspecified rakā’ah of farḍ ṣalāh, and
in all rakā’ah of Witr and nafl ṣalāh.
3) To specify the recitation for the first two rakā’ah
4) To recite al-Fātiḥah before the other sūrah
5) To place the nose with the forehead in sujūd
6) To make the second sajdah in every rakā’ah before moving to another posture
7) To perform every posture with serenity
8) The first sitting posture
9) To recite the tashahhud in it - according to the sound position
10) To recite the tashahhud in the second sitting posture
11) To stand for the third rakā’ah without delay after tashahhud
12) To say the word  ُاَ¤Uﱠ İَم , not  ُْǼْøَ¥َt

15) To specify the words of takbīr to commence every ṣalāh; this isn’t exclusively for
both the Eid prayers.
16) To recite the takbīr for rukū’ in the second rakā’ah of both Eid prayers
17) It is wājib for the Imam to recite loudly in
a) Fajr
b) The first two rakā’ah of Maghrib and ‘Ishā’ even if they are q̣aḍā’
c) In Jumu‘ah
d) In both Eid prayers

f) In Witr prayers during Ramaḍān
18) To recite quietly in Ẓuhr and ‘Aṣr, and in the remaining rakā’ah of Maghrib and

in those prayers in which the Imam recites loudly, as has the one offering optional
prayers at night.
If an individual misses the additional sūrah in the first two rakā’ah of ‘Ishā’, he will
read it aloud in the final two rakā’ah with sūrah al-Fātiḥah.
However, if he has missed sūrah al-Fātiḥah he will not repeat it in the final two
rakā’ah.

raise them adjacent to his ears. Thereafter he will say the takbīr without making madd

Arabic. However, if the person is capable (of saying the words in Arabic) it will not be
permissible to start the ṣalāh in Persian. Similarly, it is impermissible to recite in
Persian according to the soundest view.

text_raw:
The method of offering ṣalāh
A female will lower herself and attach her stomach to her thighs.
The individual will sit between the two sujūd, placing both hands on his thighs, with
total calmness.
Thereafter, he will say takbīr and proceed for the second sajdah with complete
composure and recite tasbīḥ thrice therein. As in the first sajdah, the male will keep his
stomach and thighs separated and expose his arms.
Subsequently, the individual will raise his head whilst saying the takbīr for rising up
for the second rakā’ah without taking any support from the ground with his hands
and without sitting.
The second rakā’ah will be performed in exactly the same manner as the first except
the individual will neither read thanā’ nor ta‘awwudh.
When is it sunnah to do Raf‘ al-Yadain?
Raf‘ al-Yadain (raising the hands) has been deemed sunnah in only the follow
circumstances:
1. At the beginning of every ṣalāh
2. When saying the takbīr for q̣unūt in Witr ṣalāh
3. The extra takbīr of the two Eid prayers
4. When seeing the Ka‘bah
5. When doing istilām (salutation) of the black stone
6. When standing upon mount Ṣafa
7. When standing on mount Marwah
8. When making wuq̣ūf at Arafah
9. When making wuq̣ūf at Muzdalifah
10. After pelting the Jamarat al-‘Ūlā
11. After pelting Jamarat al-Wusṭā
12. When making du‘ā’ upon completing the tasbīḥāt after ṣalāh
When the person completes both sajdah of the second rakā’ah he will spread his left
foot and sit upon it and raise the right foot. He will point his toes towards the Q̣iblah
and place his hands on his thighs whilst spreading his fingers. (A female will sit in the
tawarruk position.) The individual will read the tashahhud of ‘Ibn Masood  and
point with his index finger when saying the shahādah. The finger will be lifted at the
time of negation and dropped at the time of affirmation. Nothing more than the
tashahhud will be read in the first sitting.

text_raw:
Imāmah
To lead prayers is better than calling out adhān. To offer ṣalāh with congregation is,
without a valid excuse, sunnah for free males.
Conditions for imāmah to be correct
Six things are conditional in order for imāmah to be correct:
1) To be Muslim
2) To be mature
3) To possess a sound intellect
4) To be male
5) To be able to recite
6) To be free from disabilities (e.g. a constant nose bleed, stutter, severe lisp) and fulfil
all conditions of ṣalāh (e.g. purity and covering the satr)
Conditions for following an Imam
Fourteen things are conditional in order for following the Imam to be correct:
1) The muq̣tadī has to make an intention at the same time as his takbīr taḥrīmah.
2) It is conditional for a male to make a specific intention for imāmah (of females)
in order for the ladies’ following to be correct.
3) The Imam should be ahead of the muq̣tadī by (at least) his heels.
4) He should not be offering a prayer of a lower ranking than the muq̣tadī.
5) The Imam should not be offering a farḍ prayer different to that of the muq̣tadī.
6) The Imam should not be a muq̣īm when leading a musāfir after the time has
finished in prayers consisting of four rakā’ah
7) Neither (should the Imam be) a masbūq̣.
8) A row of females should not separate the Imam and muq̣tadī.
9) A river in which a small boat can pass -
10) And a road upon which a donkey cart can pass should not separate the Imam
and muq̣tadī.
11) Nor should a wall, due to which the movements of the Imam become
indistinguishable, come in-between the Imam and muq̣tadī. If, however, the
movements of the Imam do not become unclear due to being able to hear or
see, it will be correct to follow according to the sound position.
12) The Imam should not be mounted whilst the muq̣tadī is on foot or mounted on
another animal (mode of transport).
13) The muq̣tadī should not be in one ship whilst the Imam is in another which is
not attached to the ship of the muq̣tadī.
14) The muq̣tadī should not be aware of any matter which nullifies the wuḍū’ of
the Imam according to the belief (i.e. the madhhab) of the muq̣tadī. For
example: Flowing of blood or vomiting after which the Imam did not repeat the
wuḍū’.
Scenarios in which the muq̣tadī is in a better condition than the Imam
It is permissible for one who has performed wuḍū’ to follow one who has performed
tayammum. Similarly, it is permissible for an individual who has washed to follow one
who has made masaḥ.

text_raw:
Imāmah
A standing person may follow a seated person and a hunchback.
A person praying with indications may follow an individual like himself (i.e. someone
praying with indications).
An individual offering nafl ṣalāh may follow an individual who is offering farḍ ṣalāh.
If it becomes apparent that the Imam’s ṣalāh is null and void, the ṣalāh will have to be
repeated. It will be incumbent upon the Imam to inform the congregation to repeat
their ṣalāh to the best of his ability, according to the preferred opinion.

bab: Circumstances in which an individual is excused from attending the congregation
text_raw:
Circumstances in which an individual is excused from attending the
congregation
An individual will be excused from attending the congregation due to one of the
following eighteen things:
1. (Heavy) rainfall
2. Severe cold
3. Intense fear
4. Darkness
5. Being imprisoned
6. Being blind
7. Being paralysed
8. Missing an arm or leg
9. Illness
10. Disability (immobility)
11. Quicksand/swampy conditions
12. Chronic illness
13. Old age
14. Revising a Fiq̣h lesson with a group of people whom he will miss (i.e. he will
not have another opportunity to study with such individuals)
15. The presence of food which he strongly desires
16. Intending to travel
17. Attending to an ill person
18. Strong winds at night, not during the day
If an individual does not attend the congregation due to a valid reason which permits
missing the congregation, he will still receive the reward.

bab: The most entitled to be the Imam and the order of the rows
text_raw:
The most entitled to be the Imam and the order of the rows
If the house owner, an employed Imam or an official is not present in the
congregation, then the most knowledgeable will be most entitled to be the Imam.
Thereafter,
 The one who is the best reciter
 Then the one who is most pious
 Then the eldest
 Then one possessing the best character
 Then the most handsome
 Followed by the one noblest in lineage
 Then the one with the best voice
 Then the one with the cleanest clothes
If all are equal in the above criterion, lots will be drawn or the congregation will
choose.
However, if they differ, the individual whom the majority select will be taken into
consideration.
If they forward an Imam who is not the most appropriate, they have committed a
fault.
The imāmah of the following people is makrūh:
1. A slave
2. A blind person
3. A Bedouin
4. An illegitimate individual who is uneducated
5. An open sinner
6. An innovator.
The following things are also makrūh:
 Lengthening the ṣalāh
 Congregation of unclothed males
 Congregation of females (in general)
If females do pray in congregation, the Imam will stand in the middle (of the row not
ahead) just like unclothed people do (if they pray with congregation).
A single muq̣tadī will stand on the right of the Imam. If there is more than one
muq̣tadī, they will stand behind the Imam.
First the men will make rows, then the children, then the hermaphrodites, then the
females.

bab: What will the muq̣tadī do after the Imam completes his prayer?
text_raw:
What will the muq̣tadī do after the Imam completes his prayer?
If the Imam makes salām before the muq̣tadī completes the recitation of tashahhud he
(the muq̣tadī) will complete his tashahhud.
If the Imam raises his head before the muq̣tadī manages to read the tasbīḥ thrice in
rukū’ or sajdah, the muq̣tadī will follow the Imam.
If the Imam makes an extra sajdah or stands up after q̣ā‘idah al-akhīrah by mistake,
the muq̣tadī will not follow him.
If the Imam secures the extra rakā’ah (by making sajdah) the muq̣tadī will make salām
alone.
If the Imam stands up by mistake before sitting in q̣āԒidah al-akhīrah, the muq̣tadī will
wait for him. If the muq̣tadī makes salām before the Imam secures this extra rakā’ah
by making sajdah, the farḍ of the muq̣tadī will become null and void.
It is makrūh for the muq̣tadī to make salām after the Imam has read tashahhud but has
not yet made salām.

bab: Things which do not nullify ṣalāh
text_raw:
Things which do not nullify ṣalāh
If the individual offering ṣalāh
o looks towards some writing and understands it
o or eats something which is smaller than a chick pea from between his teeth
without excessive movement (amal-e-katheer)
o or someone passes in front of him in his place of sujūd
his ṣalāh will remain intact, though the one who passed in front of him will be sinful.
The individual’s ṣalāh will not be nullified by looking at the internal private parts of
his divorced wife, according to the preferred opinion, though raj‘ah (taking back his
wife after divorce) will be established.

Makrūh acts of ṣalāh:
Seventy seven acts are makrūh for the individual offering ṣalāh:
1. To miss a wājib intentionally
2. To miss a sunnah intentionally
3. To fiddle with one’s clothes or body
4. To brush aside pebbles except once in order to make sujūd
5. To crack the fingers
6. To interlock the fingers
7. To place the hands on the hips
8. To turn around by swivelling the neck
9. To sit with the buttocks on the ground with the knees raised
10. To place the forearms on the ground (when making sujūd)
11. To roll up the sleeves
12. To pray wearing trousers only despite being able to wear a shirt
13. To return the salām with an indication
14. To sit cross-legged without an excuse
15. To tie the hair in a bun
16. To wrap the head with a bandana and leave the middle exposed
17. To hold up one’s clothing (when going into sujūd for example)
18. To allow the clothes to droop27
19. To wrap oneself in clothing in such a manner that the individual cannot take out
his hands
20. To place the clothing under the right armpit and throw the both ends over the left
shoulder
21. To recite in any place besides the standing posture
22. To lengthen the first rakā’ah in non-compulsory prayers
23. To make the second rakā’ah longer than the first in all prayers
24. To repeat the same sūrah in the same rakā’ah of a farḍ prayer
25. To recite a sūrah which comes before a sūrah which he has already recited28
26. To skip a sūrah between two sūrahs which he reads in two consecutive rakā’ahs,
27. To sniff fragrance (intentionally)
28. To fan oneself with his clothes
29. Or (to fan oneself) with a fan once or twice29
30. To turn the fingers of the hand away from the q̣iblah in sujūd or in a any other
posture
31. To turn the toes away from the q̣iblah in sujūd or in a any other posture
32. To not place the hands on the knees in rukū’
33. To yawn
34. To close one’s eyes
35. To raise the eyes towards the sky
36. To stretch
37. To perform al-‘amal al-q̣alīl (a small amount of movement which is contrary to the
acts of ṣalāh)
38. To grip a lice
39. And to kill it
40. To cover the nose
41. To cover the mouth
27 The word ل ْF َT means to allow the clothes to droop and hang - though the clothing item is not meant to be worn in that
way. (Translator)

bab: To place a barrier and preventing the person passing in front of the praying individual
text_raw:
To place a barrier and preventing the person passing in front of the praying
individual
If it suspected that someone will pass in front of the praying individual it is preferable
to place a barrier in the ground which is as long as a dhirā‘ or more, and is as thick as a
finger.
It is sunnah to come close to it and to place it on one side. He will not pray directly
towards it.
If he cannot find something which he can place in the ground he will draw a straight
line. Some scholars say he will draw a moon-shaped semi-circle.
It is preferable to not prevent an individual passing in front of the praying person.
However, there is the option of preventing the passing person by a gesture or by
tasbīḥ. It is disliked to use both. He may prevent the passing person by raising his
voice whilst reciting.
A female may prevent the passing person by gesture or by clapping using the inner
portion of the fingers of the right hand upon the back-hand of the left. She will not
raise her voice as this is a cause of fitnah.
31 i.e. he finds it easy to recite a specific surah or he only knows this surah therefore he always recites it in ṣalāh.
(Translator)
32 i.e. he always recites the same surah because it has been established that the Prophet  used to recite this specific
surah in this ṣalāh. (ibid.)
The praying person will not wrestle with the passing person. The narrations which
mention fighting and wrestling with the passing person are interpreted that this was
permissible when movement in ṣalāh was permissible and was later abrogated.

bab: Those acts which aren’t makrūh in ṣalāh
text_raw:
Those acts which aren’t makrūh in ṣalāh
It is not makrūh:
 To tighten the waist
 To hang a sword or anything similar if he is not distracted by its movement
 To not enter the hands into the sleeves of his farjī (type of garment which has split
front and back-ends) or the slits of his jubbah according to the preferred opinion
 To face a muṣḥaf, a hanging sword, the back of a talking person, a candle or a
lantern, according to the sound position
 To make sujūd upon a carpet which has pictures without making sujūd directly on
the picture
 To kill a snake or a scorpion which he fears may harm, even if with many strikes
and turning away from the q̣iblah according to the most apparent view
There is no problem in loosening one’s clothes so they do not become entangled with
his body whilst in rukū‘ nor with wiping one’s forehead of dust and grass after
completing the prayer. If the dust or grass is harming him or distracting him from his
prayer he may wipe them off before completing his prayer. There is no problem with
looking from the corners of one’s eyes without turning the head.
There is no problem with praying on flooring, carpets and felt. However, it is best to
pray upon the earth or upon that which the earth grows (e.g. grass etc.).
There is no problem with repeating the same sūrah in two rakā’ah of nafl ṣalāh.

bab: When is it compulsory to break the prayer?
text_raw:
When is it compulsory to break the prayer?
It is compulsory to break the prayer if a distressed person calls the individual who is
praying for help, not if one of his parents call him (provided they are not in distress).
It is permissible to break the prayer due to
o An item which is valued at one dirham being stolen, even if it belongs to
someone else
o Fear of a wolf attacking sheep
o Fear of a blind person falling into a well or something similar
o If a midwife fears the new-born child will perish. Even if there is no fear of the
child perishing, the midwife may delay her ṣalāh and attend to the new-born
child. Similarly if a traveller fears thieves or highway robber, it is permissible for
him to delay the prayer of the time.
The ruling of one who discards prayer and fasting
A person who intentionally misses prayers due to laziness will be severely beaten till he
bleeds and will be imprisoned until he prays. Similar is the ruling of the one who
misses the fasts of Ramaḍān. He will not be executed unless he rejects ṣalāh or the fasts
of Ramaḍān or takes them lightly (i.e. makes a mockery of them).

text_raw:
Chapter of Witr
If he recites the q̣unūt after raising his head from rukū’ he will not have to remake
rukū’, but will make sajdah al-sahw, as q̣unūt has moved from its original place.
If the Imam goes into rukū’ before the muq̣tadī can finish du‘ā’ al-q̣unūt, or before he
even starts, and the muq̣tadī fears he will miss the rukū’, he will follow the Imam.
If the Imam doesn’t recite du‘ā’ al-q̣unūt, the muq̣tadī will recite it if it is possible for
him to then join the Imam in rukū’. If it is not possible he will follow the Imam into
rukū’ (without reciting q̣unūt).
If he joins the Imam in the rukū’ of the third rakā’ah of Witr, it will be considered that
he has also caught the q̣unūt. Therefore, he will not recite in those missed rakā’ahs
which he is making up for.
Witr will be offered in congregation in the month of Ramaḍān only. To offer Witr in
congregation in Ramaḍān is better than praying it alone in the latter part of the night,
according to the preferred view of Qādhīkhān . He says: this is the sound position.
However, others besides Qādhīkhān  have authenticated the opposite view.

text_raw:
Non-obligatory Prayers
The following prayers are sunnah al-mu’akkadah:
o Two rakā’ahs before Fajr
o Two rakā’ahs after Ẓuhr, Maghrib and ‘Ishā’
o Four rakā’ahs before Ẓuhr and before and after Jumu‘ah with one salām
The following prayers are mandūb:
o Four rakā’ahs before ‘Aṣr and ‘Ishā’
o Four rakā’ahs after ‘Ishā’
o Six rakā’ahs after Maghrib
In the first sitting of sunnah al-mu’akkadah prayers the individual will recite
tashahhud only. In the third rakā’ah he will not recite the du‘ā’ of Istiftāḥ, as opposed
to mandūb prayers.
If an individual offers a nafl prayer which consists of more than two rakā’ahs and sits
only at the end, the ṣalāh will be valid, based on the principle of istiḥsān, because all
the rakā’ahs have become like one ṣalāh and the compulsory act of sitting at the end
has been completed.
It is makrūh to read more than four rakā’ahs with one salām during the day and more
than eight rakā’ahs (with one salām) during the night. According to Imam Abū
Ḥanīfah  it is best to offer ṣalāh in sets of four both during the day and at night.
According to Ṣāḥibayn  it is better to pray in sets of two at night. The fatwa is given
according to this opinion.
The prayers of the night are more virtuous than the prayers of the day. To make
lengthy q̣iyām (standing posture) is better than making excessive sujūd.

text_raw:
Taḥiyyat al-Masjid and other prayers
To offer two rakā’ahs of Taḥiyyat al-masjid prior to sitting down is sunnah. To offer
the farḍ ṣalāh will suffice on behalf of it. Similarly any prayer offered when entering
the mosque without making the intention of Taḥiyyat al-masjid, will suffice on behalf
of it.
It is preferable to offer two rakā’ahs after wuḍū’ prior to the limbs drying, and four
rakā’ahs or more in the early morning.
The nightly prayers, Ṣalāt al-Istikhārah and Ṣalāt al-Ḥājah are all considered mandūb.
It is preferable to stay awake (for worship) on the last ten nights of Ramaḍān, the night
before the two Eids, the nights of the (first) ten days of Dhul Ḥijjah and on the night of
mid-Sha’bān (15th of Sha’ban).
It is disliked to gather in the masjid for worship on any night from amongst these
nights.

bab: Nafl ṣalāh whilst seated or mounted on a conveyance
text_raw:
Nafl ṣalāh whilst seated or mounted on a conveyance
Nafl ṣalāh whilst seated
It is permissible to offer nafl ṣalāh whilst seated despite having the capability to stand.
However, such an individual will receive half the reward of one who prays standing,
unless he has a valid excuse.33 He will sit in the same manner as tashahhud according
to the preferred opinion. It is also permissible to complete ṣalāh whilst seated after
starting ṣalāh standing according to the soundest view.34
Ṣalāh whilst mounted
A person may offer nafl ṣalāh by indications whilst mounted if he is outside the city,
facing whichever direction his conveyance is headed, even if he is offering nawāfil al-
rawātibah (sunan al-mu’akkadah). He may continue with his ṣalāh (do binā’) if he
dismounts but not if he mounts.35 It is narrated from Imam Abū Ḥanīfah  that an
individual will dismount for the sunan of Fajr as they are more emphasised than the
rest.
It is permissible for a person offering nafl ṣalāh to lean on something when tired. This
will not be makrūh. If there is no valid excuse for leaning, it will be makrūh according
to the most apparent view opinion as this is bad manners.
The presence of an impurity on the conveyance will not affect the correctness of the
ṣalāh, even if it is on the saddle or the stirrups, according to the soundest view.
The ṣalāh of a walking person is unanimously incorrect.
33 If an individual has a valid excuse due to which he prays seated, he will receive the same reward as one who prays
standing (al-Iṣbāḥ, page 258)
34 If a person starts nafl ṣalāh standing, then at some point in the ṣalāh he decides to complete the prayer whilst seated, it
will be permissible. (al-Iṣbāḥ, page 259)
35 This means that if a person started ṣalāh whilst mounted on a conveyance then dismounted, he will not have to start
ṣalāh again. Rather he can continue (do binā’). However, if a person started ṣalāh on the ground then mounted a
conveyance, his ṣalāh will become invalid. (ibid.)

bab: Farḍ and wājib ṣalāh whilst mounted
text_raw:
Farḍ and wājib ṣalāh whilst mounted
Farḍ and wājib prayers such as
 Witr
 Prayers which a person has made an oath to offer
 Those nawāfil which he started but nullified36
 Janāzah prayers
 The sajdah for an ayah which he recited on the ground
will not be correct whilst mounted on a conveyance, unless he has a valid excuse such
as
 Fear of a thief with regards to himself, his conveyance or his clothes if he
dismounts
 Fear of a predator
 Quicksand/ marshland
 Fear of the animal becoming violent and uncontrollable
 The absence of someone who may help him remount due to his inability (to mount
the animal himself).
To offer ṣalāh in a litter which is on top of a conveyance is the same as offering ṣalāh
on the conveyance itself (with regards to all the rulings mentioned above), regardless
of if the conveyance is moving or stationary. If a plank of wood is placed under the
howdah and it becomes firmly grounded, it will come under the ruling of the ground
itself. Hence, to offer farḍ ṣalāh standing inside the howdah will be correct.

text_raw:
Praying in a ship
To offer farḍ ṣalāh whilst seated with rukū’ and sujūd in a moving ship is permissible
even without an excuse, according to Imam Abū Ḥanīfah . According to Ṣāḥibayn
 to offer ṣalāh seated is impermissible, unless due to a valid excuse and this is
according to the most apparent view. Valid excuses include seasickness and inability
36 If a person starts a nafl but does not complete it, it becomes necessary for him to make up for this prayer. He cannot
make up for this nullified nafl whilst mounted. (Translator)
to disembark (get off the ship). To pray with indications is unanimously
impermissible.
A ship anchored in the middle of the ocean which is being buffeted by strong winds is
like a moving ship (with regards to the above-mentioned rulings), or else (i.e. if it is
not being buffeted by strong winds) it is like a stationary ship according to the
soundest view.
If the ship is anchored at the port, to offer ṣalāh seated (in the ship) is unanimously
impermissible. If an individual prays standing whilst the ship is partly grounded (part
of the ship is on the firmness of the land) his ṣalāh will be correct, or else (i.e. if the
ship is not partly grounded and is completely floating in the water) his ṣalāh will be
invalid according to the preferred opinion, unless it is impossible for him to
disembark.37
(If the ship is moving) the individual who is offering ṣalāh will face the q̣iblah in the
ship when he starts his prayer. Whenever the ship turns and changes direction, he too
will turn and face the q̣iblah during the ṣalāh until he completes it facing the q̣iblah.

text_raw:
Chapter regarding Tarāwīḥ
Ruling of tarāwīḥ ṣalāh
Tarāwīḥ ṣalāh is sunnah for both males and females. To offer it in congregation is
sunnat kifāyah.38
Time of tarāwīḥ ṣalāh
The time for tarāwīḥ ṣalāh (starts) after ‘Ishā’ ṣalāh. It is correct to pray Witr before or
after tarāwīḥ.
It is preferable to delay tarāwīḥ until one third or half the night has passed. It is not
makrūh to delay till later than half the night also, according to the sound position.
37 In this case it will be permissible for him to pray in the ship. (Postscript - Nūr al-Īḍāḥ, page 260)
38 If tarāwīḥ ṣalāh is not held in congregation in a particular mosque, all the attendees will be sinful. However, if a few
individuals offer the ṣalāh in congregation and the rest of the people pray individually at the homes, they will not be
sinful. (al-Iṣbāḥ, page 262)
Rakā’ahs and method of tarāwīḥ
Tarāwīḥ consists of twenty rakā’ahs with ten salāms. It is preferable to sit after every
four rakā’ahs for the duration of four rakā’ahs. Similarly (it is preferable to sit)
between the fifth tarwīḥah (set of four rakā’ahs) and the Witr ṣalāh.
Completion of the Q̣urԒān in tarāwīḥ
It is sunnah to complete a recitation of the Q̣ur’ān in tarāwīḥ ṣalāh in the month of
Ramaḍān according to the sound position. If the congregation finds this (i.e.
completion of the Q̣urԒān) tiring, the Imam will read such a portion of the Q̣urԒān
which does not repulse and distance them from attending the ṣalāh, according to the
preferred opinion.
The durūd upon The Prophet  will not be left out in any tashahhud of tarāwīḥ ṣalāh
even if the congregation finds this tiring, according to the preferred opinion.
Similarly, the thanā’ and the tasbīḥ of rukū’ and sujūd will not be left out. However,
the Imam will not read the du‘ā’ (in tashahhud before salām) if the congregation find
this wearisome.
There is no q̣aḍā’ for tarāwīḥ ṣalāh, neither alone nor in congregation.

text_raw:
Ṣalāh inside the Ka‘bah
It is correct to offer farḍ and nafl ṣalāh inside the Ka‘bah. Likewise, (it is permissible
and correct) to pray on top of it even if he does not place a barrier in front of him.
However, this (i.e. to pray on top of the Ka‘bah) is makrūh as climbing on top of the
Ka‘bah is disrespectful.
Whoever directs his back towards any other direction besides the face of his Imam
inside or above the Ka‘bah, his ṣalāh will be correct. However, if he directs his back
towards the face of his Imam his ṣalāh will not be correct.

Ṣalāh of a traveller
The minimum distance of travelling after which rulings will change is the distance
covered in three days from the shortest days of the year, when travelling at an average
pace with breaks in between. The pace of a camel and walking on foot on land and
walking on mountain pathways at a pace which suits such terrain and moderate speed
winds when travelling (by ship) on water are all considered average pace.
Shortening ṣalāh
An individual who intends to travel will shorten those farḍ ṣalāhs which consist of
four rakā’ahs - even if he has sinful intentions for travelling- once he passes the houses
of his locality and also passes the outskirts (finā’) of the locality. If the outskirts (finā’)
are detached from the locality by a field or the distance of a ghalwah (a distance of
three hundred to four hundred steps) it is not conditional to pass the outskirts.
Definition of finā’
Finā’ is an area which has been made for the benefit of the dwellers of that locality for
example a horse racing track or a cemetery.
Three things are conditional for the intention of travelling to be correct:
1. To be independent in his decisions41
2. To be bāligh
3. The journey should not be less than (the distance covered in) three days -
Therefore a person who
 Has not yet passed the buildings of his locality
 Has passed the boundaries of his locality but is a child
 Is following someone who has not made the intention to travel or intends to travel
for less than (the distance covered in) three days (and he is subject to that

his ṣalāh to be correct. If he is closer to the Ka’bah than the Imam, his ṣalāh will be invalid. (al-Iṣbāḥ, page 265)
41 This means that he makes the decisions for travelling etc. and is not dependent on someone else’s decisions. (al-Iṣbāḥ,
page 267)

master, a soldier with his superior42, may not shorten their ṣalāhs.

consideration and not the intention of the follower (who is subject to the decision of
