Ṣalāh of a traveller
reads the full four rakā’ahs and sits after two rakā’ahs his ṣalāh will be correct, though
it will be disliked. However, if he does not sit after two rakā’ahs (and stands for the
third rakā’ah without sitting for tashahhud) his ṣalāh will be invalid, unless he intends
to become a muq̣īm (resident) when standing for the third rakā’ah.44
An individual will continue to shorten his prayers until he enters his city, or makes the
intention to remain in a city or town/village for the duration of half a month. He will
continue to shorten his payers if he intends to stay for less than this, or doesn’t make
an intention whatsoever, even if he ends up staying in that place for years.
It is not correct to make the intention of being a resident of two cities without fixing
one of them for spending his nights. Similarly, it will not be correct to make the
intention of becoming a resident in a desert for anyone besides nomads. Our army (a
Muslim army) cannot make the intention of becoming residents in hostile territory
(dār al-ḥarb), nor in our own territory (dār al-Islām) when surrounding rebels.
42 All these people i.e. the female, the slave and the soldier are subject to the decision of the husband (in the case of the
female) the master (in the case of the slave) and the superior officer (in the case of the soldier.) Therefore if the husband,
master or superior officer has not made the intention to travel or has decided to travel for less than three days, they will
not shorten their ṣalāhs, even if they personally have made the intention to travel. (Translator)
43 Therefore the follower will not be required to offer full ṣalāh until he finds out that the decision maker has intended to
become a muq̣īm where they have stopped. But will it be necessary for him to ask the decision maker or not? Apparently
it will be necessary to ask. (al-Iṣbāḥ, page 267)
44 The sitting after two rakā’ahs is farḍ for a musāfir as this is his q̣āԒidah akhīrah. Therefore in the scenario where instead
of praying two rakā’ahs he prays all four, if he sits after two rakā’ahs his ṣalāh will be correct because he has completed all
the farā’iḍ, but will be disliked because he has delayed the salām which is wājib. The additional two rakā’ahs will be
considered nafl. However if he does not sit after two rakā’ahs his ṣalāh will become invalid as he has missed a farḍ.
(Translator; Radd al Muḥtār, volume 2 - with slight alterations and additions, page 610)

text_raw:
Ṣalāh of a traveller
If a traveller prays behind a resident in the correct time, the ṣalāh will be valid and he
will complete four rakā’ahs (behind the Imam). However, after the correct time has
passed it will not be valid.
In the opposite scenario (where the traveller is leading and the resident following) the
ṣalāh will be valid in and after the correct time. It is preferable for the (travelling)
Imam to say, “Complete your ṣalāh as I am a traveller”. It is more appropriate to make
this announcement before starting the ṣalāh.
The resident (who is praying behind the musāfir Imam) will not recite in those
rakā’ahs which he is completing after the musāfir Imam has concluded his ṣalāh
according to the soundest view.
The q̣aḍā’ of a prayer missed while travelling will be two rakā’ahs and the q̣aḍā’ of a
prayer missed as a resident will be four rakā’ahs. The end time will be taken into
consideration.45
A permanent place of residence (waṭn al-aṣlī) will be terminated due to (moving to)
another permanent place of residence. The waṭn al-iq̣āmah (temporary place of
residence) will be terminated by any one of the following:
 Taking up another waṭn al-iq̣āmah,
 Travelling
 Or returning to his permanent place of residence (waṭn al-aṣlī).
Definition of waṭn al-aṣlī
1) The place where an individual was born
2) Where he/she married46
3) Intends to live there permanently.
Definition of waṭn al-iq̣āmah
A place where a person intends to reside for half a month or more.
The research scholars have not taken waṭn al-suknā into consideration. This is that
place where a person intends to reside for less than half a month.
45 This means that at the end of that specific prayer time if he is a musāfir he will perform q̣aḍā’ of two rakā’ahs and if he
is a muq̣īm he will perform four rakā’ahs. (al-Iṣbāḥ, page 269)
46 For example, if a lady from London gets married to a man from Dewsbury and moves there after marriage, Dewsbury
will now be considered her waṭn al-aṣlī. (Translator)

bab: The ṣalāh of an ill person
text_raw:
The ṣalāh of an ill person
If a person is completely unable to stand or it is extremely difficult, due to severe pain
or fears the illness will worsen or extend (due to standing), he will pray seated with
proper rukū’ and sujūd. He may sit as he wishes according to the soundest view. If it is
not completely impossible for him to stand, he will stand for as long possible.
If the individual is unable to make rukū’ and sujūd he will pray seated with
indications. His indication for sujūd will be lower (i.e. he will lower his head more)
than his indication for rukū’. Nothing (for example a plank of wood) will be raised up
to his face in order for him to prostrate upon it. However, if this is done (i.e. if
something is raised up to his face) and he bowed his head, his sajdah will be valid or
else it will be invalid.
If it is difficult for the individual to sit he will pray with indications whilst lying flat on
his back or on one side. The first of these two postures is preferred. A pillow/cushion
will be placed under his head so that his face is directed towards the q̣iblah and not the
sky. It is appropriate that his knees are raised if possible so that his feet are not
stretched out directly towards the q̣iblah.
If making indications is also impossible, his prayers will be postponed as long as he
understands speech (i.e. is in his senses).47 It is mentioned in al-Hidāyah that this is
the sound position.
In al-Tajnīs wa al-Mazīd48 the author of al-Hidāyah has emphatically mentioned that
the duty of making up for missed prayers (q̣aḍā’) will be dropped if the individual’s
inability to make indications remains for more than five prayers even if he can
understand speech (i.e. is in his senses). This view has been authenticated by
Qādhīkhān and a similar ruling is to be found in al-Muḥīṭ. Both Shaikh al-Islām
47 This mas’alah has four scenarios: 1) if his inability continues for six prayers in the state that he is completely unaware
of what is going on around him: unanimously he will not have to make up for these missed prayers.  2) If he misses less
than six prayers in the condition that he is aware of what is going on around him: unanimously he will make up for these
missed prayers. 3) If his inability remains for six prayers but he is aware of what is going on around him and 4) if his
inability remains for less than six prayers but he is unaware of his surroundings: the mashāyikh differ with regards to

bab: The ṣalāh of an ill person
text_raw:
The ṣalāh of an ill person
these final two scenarios. Some say that he will have to make up for the missed prayers (this is the opinion of the author
of al-Hidāyah) whilst others say that he will not have to make up for the missed prayers (this is the opinion of al-Bazdawī
al-Ṣaghīr). (al-Iṣbāḥ - with slight alterations and additions, page 267)
48 Another book by the author of al-Hidāyah. (Translator)
(Khāhirzādah) and Fakhr al-Islām (al-Sarakhsī) have preferred this opinion. It is
mentioned in Al-Ẓahīriyyah that this is the ẓāhir al-riwāyah and the fatwa is given
upon this view. It is mentioned in al-Khulāṣah that this is the preferred opinion and
this view has been authenticated in al-Yanābī‘ and in al-Badāi‘. Al-Walwāliji has
decisively given the same opinion. May Allāh have mercy upon them all.49
He will not make indications with his heart, his eyes or his eyebrows.
If the individual is capable of standing but is unable to make rukū’ and sujūd he will
pray seated with indications.
If he is afflicted by an illness (whilst in ṣalāh) he will complete the ṣalāh however
possible, even if (he has to complete the prayer) with indications, according to the
prominent opinion.
If an individual is praying whilst seated with proper rukū’ and sujūd and then
becomes well (i.e. he gains the strength to stand and pray) he may continue his ṣalāh.
However, if he is praying with indications, he cannot continue his ṣalāh.50
Whoever remains insane or unconscious for the five prayers will have to make up for
these missed prayers (i.e. make q̣aḍā’). If he remains in this condition for more than
this (i.e. five prayers) he will not have to make q̣aḍā’.

bab: When will a person be absolved of missed prayers and fasts?
text_raw:
When will a person be absolved of missed prayers and fasts?
If an ill person dies whilst being unable to offer ṣalāh with indications he does not have
to make a bequest regarding his missed prayers even if they (the missed prayers) are
less (than six).
Similarly, if a traveller or an ill person does not fast and passes away before becoming a
resident (in the case of the traveller) or before becoming well (in the case of the ill
person), he will not have to make a bequest regarding his missed fasts.
49 The author here has extensively quoted other reliable works of Hanafi fiq̣h to substantiate his position on this
mas’alah. (ibid.)
50 If a person initially prays with indications and then during his ṣalāh he becomes well and gains the strength to pray
fully, it will not be permissible for him to continue his prayer. Rather he must start his prayer anew. (al-Iṣbāḥ - with slight
alterations and additions, page 273)
An individual will have to make a bequest/testament for all those fasts and prayers
which he had the capability of carrying out but they still remain a debt upon him.51
His walī (heir) will take out half a ṣā‘52 of wheat or its equivalent in money for every
fast and every prayer missed, including Witr, from one third of whatever wealth the
deceased person has left behind.
If the deceased person has not made a bequest/testament and the heir pays on behalf
of the deceased individual out of goodwill, it will be permissible. However it is not
correct for the heir to fast or pray on the deceased’s behalf.
If the amount which the deceased has bequeathed is not sufficient to fulfil the fidyah
which is compulsory upon him, this (insufficient) amount will be given to a poor
person and thereby the deceased person will be absolved of (as many prayers and fasts
that are covered by) this amount. Thereafter the poor person will gift this amount back
to the heir who will take possession of it. The heir will then give the amount back to
the poor person and the deceased person again will be absolved of (as many prayers
and fasts that are covered by) this amount. Thereafter the poor person will gift this
amount back to the heir who will take possession of it. The heir will then give the
amount back to the poor person and again the deceased person will be absolved of (as
many prayers and fasts that are covered by) this amount. This process will be repeated
until the deceased person is absolved of all the prayers and fast which are a debt upon
him.

text_raw:
Q̣aḍā’ of missed prayers
To maintain correct sequence between
 A missed prayer and a prayer being offered in its correct time
 And between many missed prayers
is necessary.
This sequence will be dropped due to one of three things:
1. If the mustaḥab time (to offer the prayer of that time) is tight53, according to the
soundest view
2. Forgetfulness
3. If the missed prayers total six excluding Witr. Witr will not cause the sequence to
drop though it is necessary to pray it in correct order.54
The (need to pray in) order will not return due to the missed prayers coming down to
less than six55  nor due to recently missing a prayer after missing six (or more) prayers
in the past56. This is the soundest view in both scenarios.
If a person offers a farḍ prayer whilst remembering that he has a missed prayer to
make up for, even if that missed prayer is Witr, the farḍ ṣalāh (which he has just
offered) will be invalid (fāsid). However, this invalidation is suspended and pending. If
the time for the fifth prayer after the missed prayer elapses, whilst remembering that
he has a missed prayer to make up for, all the prayers will be considered correct.

there is only so much time left from the mustaḥab time of ‘Aṣr that the individual can only offer one of the two (either
the missed Ẓuhr or the ‘Aṣr in its time) he will pray the ‘Aṣr ṣalāh and offer the missed Ẓuhr thereafter. (Translator)
54 This means that Witr will not be counted in those six prayers which result in the tartīb (sequence) being dropped.
However, if a person has missed less than six prayers, he will have to maintain the correct sequence of offering Witr ṣalāh
after ‘Ishā’ and before Fajr. (ibid.)
55 For example if a person misses the prayers of a full month then makes up for all of them besides one or two prayers, he
will not have to read the remaining missed prayers in order despite the fact that they now number less than six. (al-Iṣbāḥ
- with slight alterations and additions, page 275)

pray and then, after some time, misses a few (less than six) prayers, he will not have to pray them in order. Rather they
will be added onto the one month’s worth of missed prayers. (ibid.)
Hence these prayers will not become invalid by making up for the missed prayer

Joining the farḍ prayer
If an individual starts a farḍ prayer alone and then the jamā‘ah (congregation) for that
prayer is started, he will break his prayer and join the congregation, provided he has
not yet prostrated (made sajdah) for his own individual prayer, or has prostrated in all
those prayers which consist of less than four rakā’ahs.
If the individual has made sajdah in a prayer which consists of four rakā’ahs, he will
offer an additional rakā’ah and end his prayer with salām, so that these two rakā’ahs
which he has offered become nafl. Thereafter he will join the congregation to complete
his farḍ.
If he has already prayed three rakā’ahs (in a prayer which consists of four rakā’ahs), he
will complete the prayer, and join the congregation as one reading nafl ṣalāh, except in
the case of ‘Aṣr ṣalāh (as it is impermissible to offer nafl ṣalāh after the farḍ of ‘Aṣr).
If an individual has stood up for the third rakā’ah and the congregation has started
before he makes sajdah for it (i.e. the third rakā’ah), he will end his ṣalāh by making
salām whilst standing according to the soundest view.
If an individual is in the midst of offering the sunnah prayers before Jumu‘ah and the
khaṭīb makes his appearance, or is offering his sunan before Ẓuhr, he will make salām
after two rakā’ahs (and join the congregation.) This is according to the most apparent
view. The individual will make up for the sunnah prayers after completing the farḍ.
If an individual attends the mosque and finds the Imam in the farḍ prayer, he will
immediately join the congregation and will not busy himself with the sunnah prayers,
except in Fajr ṣalāh. If he is confident he will not miss the Fajr congregation, he will
pray the sunan before joining the Imam, and if he is not confident he will leave them
(i.e. the sunnats before Fajr).
The sunnats of Fajr ṣalāh will not be made up for unless they were missed with the farḍ
prayer itself.
An individual will make up for the sunan before Ẓuhr (if he has missed them) before
the two rakā’ahs of sunnah after the farḍ, in the prescribed time for Ẓuhr.
An individual who caught only one rakā’ah of Ẓuhr will not be considered to have
prayed in congregation59, though he has achieved the virtue. There is a difference of
opinion with regards to an individual who joins the congregation in the third rakā’ah.
If an individual is confident the prescribed time will not elapse (pass), he may offer

Whoever finds the Imam in rukū’ and says takbīr and remains standing until the
Imam raises his head, he has not caught the rakā’ah.
If an individual goes into rukū’ before his Imam, after the Imam has recited a
sufficient amount whereby ṣalāh becomes correct, the individual’s rukū’ will only be
valid if the Imam joins him in rukū’. If, however, the Imam does not join him in rukū’,
his rukū’ will become invalid.
It is makrūh to exit from a masjid in which adhān has already been called until the
individual prays, unless he is responsible for a different congregation.
It is not makrūh if an individual exits after offering the prayer alone, unless the
congregation is about to start before he exits in Ẓuhr and ‘Ishā’. In both these prayers
he will join the congregation as one praying nafl.
After offering a prayer, an individual will not pray another similar prayer.60
59 Hence if an individual made an oath that he will not pray Ẓuhr ṣalāh behind an Imam and comes and joins the
congregation in the final rakā’ah, his oath will not be broken because he has missed the majority of the ṣalāh (three
rakā’ahs) with the Imam. (al-Iṣbāḥ - with slight alterations, page 279)
60 These are the wordings of a hadith and there is a difference of opinion with regards to their interpretation. A few
interpretations are: a) an individual should not repeat a prayer in hope of more reward b) a person should not repeat the
prayer due to a mere suspicion that his prayer was incorrect c) a second congregation resembling the first should not be
held in one masjid. (For more interpretations see al-Iṣbāḥ, page 280)

Sujūd al-sahw
Two sajdahs are necessary with tashahhud and salām due to missing out a wājib act
forgetfully, even if it reoccurs.61
If a person intentionally neglects a wājib act he will be sinful and will have to repeat his
ṣalāh to make up for the deficiency.
In the case where the individual has intentionally neglected the wājib he will not make
sujūd al-sahw, except in three circumstances, as mentioned by some scholars:
1. Neglecting the first sitting,
2. Delaying one sajdah from the first rakā’ah till the end of the ṣalāh
3. Or daydreaming intentionally so much so that he is distracted from performing a
rukn.
It is sunnah to offer the sujūd al-sahw after the salām and one salām to the right is
sufficient according to the soundest view. It is makrūh tanzīhī to perform the sajdah
before salām.
A person will not be required to perform sujūd al-sahw
 If the sun rises after making salām in Fajr ṣalāh
 Becomes red in colour during (the time of) ‘Aṣr
 Due to such an occurrence which prevents the individual from doing binā’ (for
example, breaking one’s wuḍū’ intentionally)
The muq̣tadī will have to perform sujūd al-sahw due to a mistake made by his Imam,
not due to his own mistake (i.e. if he is praying behind an Imam and he forgets one of
the wājibāt, he will not have to make sujūd al-sahw).
A masbūq̣ (a person who joined the ṣalāh after a rakā’ah or more had already been
performed) will perform sujūd with the Imam then stand to complete the rakā’ah
which he had missed. If the masbūq̣ makes a mistake whilst making up for the missed
rakā’ahs he will perform sujūd al-sahw, but not a lāḥiq̣.
The Imam will not make sujūd al-sahw in Jumu‘ah and Eid prayers.

text_raw:
Doubt in ṣalāh
If a person has doubt regarding how many rakā’ahs he has offered before completing
the ṣalāh, and this is the first time he has experienced such doubt, or this is unusual for
him, his ṣalāh will become invalid.
If a doubt arises after he has made salām it will not be taken into consideration unless
he becomes certain that he has missed an act of ṣalāh.
If a person is prone to doubt (in ṣalāh) he will act upon the notion he is more inclined
to (al-ẓann al-ghālib). If a person is not inclined to any specific notion he will take the
least (amount of rakā’ahs which he thinks he may have offered), and will sit after every
rakā’ah which he thinks could perhaps be the last.

Sajdat al-tilāwah
The cause (for having to perform sajdat al-tilāwah) is reciting (a sajdah ayah) upon
both the reciter and the person who hears him recite according to the sound position.
Sajdat al-tilāwah is a wājib which may be delayed if the reciter is not in ṣalāh, though it
is makrūh tanzīhī to delay it. It will become wājib upon the person who recites a
sajdah ayah even if in Persian (i.e. any other language besides Arabic.)
To recite the word of sajdah with one word before or after it from the very same ayah
is like reading the full ayah according to the sound position.
There are fourteen āyāt of sajdah in the following sūrahs:
1) al-A‘rāf  2) al-Ra’d  3) al-Naḥl  4) al-Isrā’  5) Maryam  6) the former in al-Ḥajj
7) al-Furq̣ān    8)  al-Naml  9) al-Sajdah  10) Ṣād  11) Ḥā Mīm Sajdah  12) al-Najm
13) al-Inshiq̣āq̣    14) Iq̣ra’
Sajdah will become wājib upon everyone who hears one of these verses even if he has
no intention of hearing it except for
 A female who is menstruating
 (A female who) is in the state of nifās
 An Imam and the one praying behind him63
If the Imam and the muq̣tadīs hear the āyah from someone else (who is not a muq̣tadī)
they will make sajdah after completing the ṣalāh. If they make sajdah in the ṣalāh it will
not be sufficient though their ṣalāh will not become invalid according to the ẓāhir al-
riwāyah.
Sajdat al-tilāwah will become necessary due to hearing the verse being recited in
Persian (i.e. any other language besides Arabic) if the listener understands it,
according to the correct opinion.
Different views have been authenticated with regards to sajdat al-tilāwah becoming
wājib due to hearing a sajdah verse being recited by a sleeping person or an insane
person. (Some scholars are of the opinion that sajdah will become wājib while others
opine that it will not.)
Sajdah will not become necessary due to hearing it from a bird (parrot etc.) or due to
hearing an echo (of the ayah).
The sajdat al-tilāwah will be fulfilled by making (an extra) rukū’ or sajdah in ṣalāh,
besides the rukū’ and sajdah for that ṣalāh.
The rukū’ of the ṣalāh will suffice on behalf of the sajdat al-tilāwah provided the reciter
makes the intention (of sajdah al-tilāwah when going into rukū’) and the sajdah of
ṣalāh will suffice on behalf of sajdat al-tilāwah even if the individual doesn’t make an
intention, if the flow of recitation is not halted by more than two verses.64

Sujūd al-tilāwah
63 If an Imam is leading prayer and a muq̣tadī recites an ayah of sajdah, the Imam and the muq̣tadīs will not have to
perform sujūd al-tilāwah. (al-Iṣbāḥ, page 287)
64 If the reciter continues and recites more than two verses after the verse of sujūd, the rukū’ and sujūd of ṣalāh will not be
sufficient on behalf of that sujūd al-tilāwah. (Translator)
If an individual hears the ayah being recited by an Imam but does not join him in
ṣalāh, or joins him in a different rakā’ah, he will perform the sajdah outside ṣalāh,
according to the most apparent view.
If the individual joins the ṣalāh before the Imam makes the sajdat al-tilāwah, he will
perform sajdah with him (i.e. with the Imam).
If the individual joins the Imam after he (i.e. the Imam) has performed the sajdat al-
tilāwah, in the same rakā’ah, it will be considered that he has performed the sajdat al-
tilāwah as well. Therefore he will not have to make sajdah.
Those sajdat al-tilāwah which are to be performed in ṣalāh will not be made up for
outside ṣalāh.
If a person recites an ayah of sujūd outside ṣalāh and performs sajdat al-tilāwah for it,
and then reads the same ayah again in ṣalāh, he will have to perform sujūd once again.
If he did not perform sujūd the first time (when he recited the ayah outside ṣalāh), one
sujūd (the one performed in ṣalāh) will be sufficient, according to the ẓāhir al-riwāyah.
Similarly, the person who repeatedly recites one verse of sajdah in the same place (one
sujūd will be sufficient for him), not one who reads it in different places. (This
individual will have to make a separate sajdah for every majlis (place) where he recited
the āyah of sujūd.)
The place (majlis) is considered to have changed
 By moving from that place, even if he moves to weave fabric65
 By moving from one branch to another (if he is reciting in a tree)
 And swimming in a river or large reservoir
according to the soundest view.
The majlis will not change due to the following actions in the place where he is
reciting:
 Moving to the different corners of one room or masjid even if it (the room or
masjid) is large
 The travelling of a ship
65 In past times fabric was woven by embedding two sticks in the ground some distance apart and weaving the thread
between these two sticks. If a person recites an ayah of sujūd while standing by one of the sticks and he moves to the
other stick and re-reads this ayah, he will have to perform sujūd twice as the majlis has changed. (Translator)

text_raw:
Sujūd al-tilāwah
 Offering one or two rakā’ahs
 Drinking
 Eating two morsels
 Walking two steps
 Leaning
 Sitting down (from a standing position)
 Standing up
 Mounting (a mode of transport)
 Descending from a mode of transport
 Travelling of an animal (mode of transport) whilst the reciter is praying ṣalāh.
The need to make sajdah will reoccur upon the listener due to him changing location,
even if the reciter remains in one place. In the opposite scenario66, the listener will not
have to remake sujūd according to the soundest view.
It is makrūh to recite a sūrah and leave out the ayah of sajdah. The opposite (to only
recite the ayah of sajdah) is not makrūh. It is preferable to recite an ayah or more in
addition to the ayah of sajdah and to recite it quietly in the presence of one who is not
prepared to make sajdah. It is also preferable to stand up and then go into prostration.
The listener will not raise his head from sujūd before the reciter. However the reciter
will not be commanded to go forward, and nor will the listeners be commanded to
make rows. Rather every individual will prostrate as he is.
The conditions for sajdat al-tilāwah to be correct are the same as the conditions for
ṣalāh besides takbīr of taḥrīmah.
The method of sajdat al-tilāwah
Its method is to make one sajdah between two takbīrs (these two takbīrs are sunnah)
without raising the hands and without reciting tashahhud and without making salām.
66 In the scenario where the listener remains in the same position and the reciter is moving from place to place, the
listener will only have to perform sujūd once. (ibid.)

text_raw:
Prostration of gratitude (sajdat al-shukr)
Prostration of gratitude is disliked according to Imam Abū Ḥanīfah  and the
individual will not be rewarded for it. Rather it is better not to make prostration of
gratitude.
According to Imam Abū Yūsuf and Imam Muḥammad , it is a commendable act for
which the individual will be rewarded.
The method of sajdat al-shukr is the same as sujūd al-tilāwah.

text_raw:
An important point for the fulfilment of all necessities
Imam al-Nasafī  has mentioned in his book al-Kāfī: whoever recites all the verses of
sujūd in one sitting and then makes sujūd for every verse, Allāh will suffice for his
every need.

text_raw:
Jumu‘ah
The Jumu‘ah prayer is farḍ ‘ain upon every individual who meets seven criteria:
1. To be male
2. To be a free person
3. To be a resident in a city or in such a place which is included in the definition of
being a resident in a city, according to the soundest view
4. To be healthy
5. Secure from a tyrant
6. Soundness of both eyes
7. Soundness of both legs
Six things are conditional for Jumu‘ah to be correct:
1. A city or its outskirts
2. A ruler or his deputy
3. The time of Ẓuhr; therefore Jumu‘ah prayer will not be correct before Ẓuhr time
sets in and the Jumu‘ah prayer will be nullified by Ẓuhr time finishing.
4. The sermon before the prayer with the intention of giving a sermon, in the time of
Jumu‘ah, and the presence of at least one individual to hear it from amongst those
people with whom Jumu‘ah prayer may be conducted (these people will be
mentioned soon) according to the sound position
5. Open permission (for anyone to attend)
6. A congregation; this will consist of (a minimum) of three men besides the Imam,
even if they are slaves, travellers or ill. It is conditional that the congregation
remains with the Imam until he prostrates. If they desert the Imam after he has
performed sujūd, the Imam will complete the ṣalāh alone as Jumu‘ah. However if
they desert him before he prostrates, the Jumu‘ah prayer will become null and
void.
The Jumu‘ah ṣalāh cannot be conducted with a female or child, in addition to two
men.
It is permissible for a slave or an ill person to lead the Jumu‘ah prayer.
Definition of a city: every place which has a muftī, a leader and a Q̣āḍi who enforces
the rulings and imposes the shar‘ī punishments, and the buildings in that place are
equivalent in number to the buildings of Mina, according to the ẓāhir al-riwāyah. If
the Q̣āḍi or the leader is also a muftī, there is no need for numbers (i.e. there is no
need for another separate mufti).
Jumu‘ah prayer is permissible in Minā in the Hajj season for the caliph or the leader of
Ḥijāz.
It is correct to suffice on one tasbīḥ or taḥmīd in the khuṭbah, though it is disliked.
There are eighteen sunan of khuṭbah:
1. To be in the state of purity
2. To cover the satr
3. To sit on the pulpit (minbar) before starting the khuṭbah
4. To call the adhān from in front of the Imam and similarly the iq̣āmah
5. To then stand with the sword in the left hand whilst leaning upon it in every city
which had been conquered forcefully,

Jumu‘ah
6. And (to stand) without a sword in those lands which were conquered through a
truce
7. To face the congregation
8. To start with ḥamd (praise) and thanā’ of Allāh  as is befitting to Him
9. To recite the shahādatain
10. To send salutations upon the Prophet 
11. To advise and remind
12. To recite a verse of the Qur’ān
13. To give two sermons
14. To sit between the two sermons
15. To repeat ḥamd, thanā’ and salutations upon the Prophet  at the beginning of
the second sermon
16. To make du‘ā’ for all believing men and women in the second sermon by asking
forgiveness for them
17. To deliver the sermon to the congregation in such a manner that they can hear
18. To shorten the sermon to the length of a sūrah from the ṭiwāl al-mufaṣṣal
It is makrūh to lengthen the khuṭbah and to miss out one of the sunan.
It is incumbent to set off for Jumu‘ah and to leave all business transactions with the
first adhān according to the soundest view.
Once the Imam comes out there is no ṣalāh and no talking. An individual must not
reply to salām, nor to a sneeze until he finishes the Jumu‘ah prayer.
It is makrūh for the one present in the sermon to:
 Eat
 Drink
 Fiddle
 Turn around
The person delivering the sermon (khaṭīb) will not make salām to the congregation
once he ascends the minbar.
It is makrūh to leave the city once the adhān has been called before offering the prayer.
If an individual who does not have to pray Jumu‘ah does pray it, it will suffice for the
farḍ of that time (and he will not have to offer Ẓuhr).
If a person who does not have a valid excuse (for not praying Jumu‘ah) offers Ẓuhr
ṣalāh before Jumu‘ah it will be impermissible. If he then sets off towards the prayer
whilst the Imam is still engaged in it, his Ẓuhr will become invalid even if he does not
manage to catch the Jumu‘ah prayer.
It is makrūh for those excused from attending Jumu‘ah and prison inmates to perform
Ẓuhr with congregation in the city on Friday.
Whoever manages to join the Jumu‘ah ṣalāh in tashahhud or in sujūd al-sahw, he will
complete the prayer as Jumu‘ah.

The two Eids
The Eid prayer is wājib, according to the soundest view, on that individual upon
whom Jumu‘ah is wājib, with all its prerequisites besides khuṭbah. Eid prayer will be
correct without a khuṭbah though this is disapproved, as is delivering the sermon
before the Eid prayer.
Thirteen acts are mandūb (preferred) in Eid al-Fitr:
1) To eat something (before setting off for the Eid prayer), preferably an odd amount
of dates
2) To have a bath
3) To use miswāk
4) To apply fragrance
5) To wear ones best clothes
6) To pay the sadaq̣at al-fitr if it is wājib upon him
7) To express joy and happiness
8) To give as much charity as possible
9) To wake up early
10) To set off early to the muṣallā
11) To pray Fajr ṣalāh in one’s local masjid
12) And to then set off for the muṣallā on foot whilst reciting takbīr quietly. The
individual will stop reciting takbīr upon reaching the muṣallā according to one
narration and according to another narration, when he starts ṣalāh.
13) To return via a different route
It is makrūh to offer nafl prayers before Eid prayer in the muṣallā and at home. After
Eid ṣalāh it is makrūh to perform nafl prayers in the muṣallā only, according to the
preferred opinion of the majority.
Time for Eid prayer
(In order for Eid prayer to be correct it must be performed) from once the sun has
risen a spears length or two spears length until zawāl.
Method of performing Eid ṣalāh
a) Make the intention of Eid prayer
b) Say the takbīr of taḥrīmah
c) Recite thanā’
d) Make the three extra takbīrs, raising the hands each time
e) Recite ta‘awwudh
f) Recite Bismillāh quietly
g) Recite Fātiḥah and another sūrah. It is preferable to recite

The two Eids
 Delay eating till after the prayer
 Recite the takbīr loudly on the way to the muṣallā
 Explain the rulings of sacrifice and takbīr al-tashrīq̣ in the sermon
 And the prayer may be delayed for three days due to an excuse
To act out the scene of the plain of ‘Arafah is baseless.67

day once after every farḍ ṣalāh performed with a mustaḥab congregation upon a
resident Imam and all those praying behind him, even if they are travellers, slaves or
females, according to Imam Abū Ḥanīfah .
Ṣāḥibayn  say: it is wājib to read the takbīr immediately after every farḍ prayer upon
everyone who offers it, even if he is praying alone, is a traveller or a villager, until the
‘Aṣr of the fifth day from the day of ‘Arafah. This is the opinion which is acted upon
and the fatwa is given according to it.
There is no problem in reciting the takbīr after the Eid prayer.

Prayers for solar and lunar eclipses and the prayers for fear
Two rakā’ahs have been made sunnah in the same manner as nafl prayers for a solar
eclipse, with the Imam who leads the Jumu‘ah, or someone who has been appointed
by the ruler, without adhān, iq̣āmah, reciting loudly and without a sermon. Rather an
announcement will be made

the Imam will supplicate whilst seated facing the q̣iblah if he wishes, or standing facing
the congregation (this is preferred). The people will say āmīn upon his supplication,

Istisq̣ā’
There will be individual prayers and repentance for istisq̣ā’ (seeking rain from Allāh).
It is preferred to go out (into the open to pray for rain) for three days on foot, wearing
washed clothes which are old or patched, expressing helplessness, humility and
modesty in front of Allāh , exposing the head and giving charity daily before setting
off.
It is preferable to take out animals, elderly people and children also.
In Makkah and Bait al-Maq̣dis the people will gather in Masjid al-Ḥaram and in
Masjid al-Aqsa. This is preferable for the people of Medina also (i.e. they should
gather in the Prophet’s mosque).
The Imam will stand facing the q̣iblah with his hands raised and the people will sit
facing the q̣iblah and say āmīn upon the Imam’s supplication. The Imam will make
the following supplication:

text_raw:
Ṣalāh of fear
It is permissible to offer the prayer of fear if an enemy is present, or there is a fear of
drowning of burning.
Method of performing the ṣalāh of fear
1. If the congregation disputes about praying behind one Imam (i.e. all of them want
to pray behind one Imam), he (the Imam) will split them into two groups: one will
be made to face the enemy, whilst he leads the second group for one rakā’ah (if it is
a ṣalāh which consists of two rakā’ahs) or two rakā’ahs (if the ṣalāh consists of four
rakā’ahs or in Maghrib ṣalāh).
2. Then this group (which has already offered some rakā’ahs with the Imam) will go
to face the enemy on foot, and the other group will come (to join the Imam). The
Imam will offer the remaining rakā’ahs with this second group. The Imam will
make salām alone and this second group will go back to face the enemy.
3. Thereafter the first group will return and complete the remainder of their prayer
without q̣irā’ah and then they will make salām and return to face the enemy.
4. After this the second group will return. If they wish they may complete their
remaining rakā’ahs with q̣irā’ah.
If the fear intensifies, everyone will pray individually with indications, whilst
mounted, towards any direction possible.
The ṣalāh of fear is not permissible if there is no enemy present.
It is preferable to carry weapons in ṣalāh of fear.
If the congregation do not dispute about praying behind one Imam, it is better that
each group prays behind separate imams, as in the normal situation of security and
safety.

Rulings of janāzah
It is sunnah to face a person in the throes of death (who is about to die) towards the
q̣iblah on his right side. It is permissible to lay him flat on his back. His head will be
lifted slightly and he will be indirectly instructed (to recite the shahādatain) by
mentioning them in his presence without being forceful.68 However, the dying person
will not be commanded to recite the shahādatain.
To make talq̣īn after burial is permissible in the sharī‘ah. According to one opinion
talq̣īn will not be made whilst according to another opinion an individual will not be
commanded to make talq̣īn, nor will he be prevented from doing so.
It is preferable that the relatives and neighbours of the dying person come to his
presence and recite Sūrah Yāsīn and, preferably, Sūrah al-Ra‘d. The scholars differ as
to whether a menstruating female or a female in the state of nifās (post-natal bleeding)
will be made to leave from the presence of the dying person.
Once a person dies his jaw-bone will be tied and his eyelids will be closed. The
individual closing the eyelids will say:

text_raw:
Rulings of janāzah
water into the nostrils, unless he is in the state of janābah. Water which has been
boiled with lotus or ḥurḍ leaves will be poured over the body (if available) or else pure
water will be used.
The head and the beard of the deceased individual will be washed with khiṭmī
(marshmallow - althea officinalis). Thereafter he will be made to lie on his left side and
will be bathed until the water reaches that part of his body which is resting on the
plank. The same procedure will be followed for his right side.
Then the deceased person will be made to sit up propped against the person bathing
him, and his stomach will be stroked gently. Whatever comes out from it will be
washed and the full bath will not be repeated.
Thereafter, the body will be dried with a piece of cloth. Ḥanūṭ (embalmment) will be
applied to his beard and head and camphor will be applied to the body-parts which
touch the floor in sujūd.
Cotton will not be used in the bathing process, according to the ẓāhir al-riwāyah, and
nor will the hair and nails of the deceased be clipped. The hair and beard will not be
combed.
A female may bathe her deceased husband as opposed to a male (i.e. a male cannot
bathe his deceased wife). Similarly, an umm al-walad (a female slave with whom the
master has had a child) may not bathe her deceased master.
If a female dies in the company of men (and there are no females present) they will
give her tayammum using a cloth, as in the opposite scenario (i.e. if a male dies in the
company of females and there aren’t any males who may bathe him). If a blood
relative (dhū raḥm maḥram) is present (in either scenario), he/she will give the
deceased tayammum without using a cloth.
Similarly, a khunthā mushkil (indistinguishable hermaphrodite) will be given
tayammum according to the ẓāhir al-riwāyah.
It is permissible for males and females to bath deceased boys and girls, provided they
do not feel any lust.
There is no problem in kissing a deceased person.
It is the responsibility of the husband to make the funeral arrangements of his wife
even if he is poor, according to the soundest view.
If the deceased has no wealth, making the funeral arrangements will be the
responsibility of the one who was responsible for the deceased’s expenditure (from
amongst his relatives). If the person who was responsible for the deceased’s
expenditure is unavailable, burial arrangements will be made from the bait al-māl

text_raw:
Rulings of janāzah
(public treasury). If the bait al-māl does not pay for the burial due to being unable or
due to being oppressive, it is the responsibility of the people to make the burial
arrangements.
An individual who is unable to make burial arrangements will ask others on behalf of
the deceased to assist in the arrangements.
The sunnah shroud for a male consists of
1) The q̣amīṣ
2) The izār
3) The lifāfah
made of those materials which the deceased used to wear in his lifetime.
The kifāyah (minimum which will suffice) shroud for the male consists of
1) The izār
2) The lifāfah
A white cotton shroud is preferred.
Both the izār and the lifāfah will extend from the head till the feet.
The q̣amīṣ will not have sleeves, side pieces (which are inserted to widen the qamees)
or pockets and the ends will not be tied. It is disliked to include a turban (in the
shroud) according to the soundest view.
The shroud will be wrapped from the left first then the right. The shroud may be tied if
there is a fear of it coming loose.
In the sunnah shroud for a female that the khimār be inserted to cover her face (and
head), and another cloth to tie her breasts, in addition (to the three cloths mention in
the sunnah shroud for a male).
In the kifāyah shroud for a female, a khimār will be inserted, in addition (to the two
pieces of cloth mentioned in the kifāyah shroud for a male).
The hair of the deceased female will be divided into two bunches and placed upon her
chest, above the q̣amīṣ. The khimār will come on top of that, beneath the lifāfah. The
piece of cloth used to tie the breasts will come after that.
The shroud will be fumed with scents an odd number of times before enshrouding the
deceased individual in it.
The shroud in a dire situation (when a suitable shroud is unavailable) will be whatever
is found.

text_raw:
The janāzah prayer
To perform the janāzah ṣalāh upon the dead is farḍ kifāyah.
The arkān of janāzah ṣalāh:
1. The takbīrs
2. And to stand.
There are six conditions for janāzah ṣalāh:
1) The deceased individual must be a Muslim,
2) He (the deceased) must be in the state of purity,
3) The dead body must be in front (of the congregation),
4) The dead body, or most of it, or half of it with the head, must be present,
5) The individual offering the janāzah prayer must not be mounted without an
excuse
6) And the dead body must be upon the ground; if the dead body is on an animal
(or a vehicle) or is being held by people, the prayer will not be valid according
to the preferred opinion, unless due to a valid reason.
There are four sunan of janāzah ṣalāh:
1) The Imam should stand in line with the chest of the dead body, whether the
deceased is a male or a female
2) To recite thanā after the first takbīr
3) To send salutations upon the Prophet  after the second
4) And to supplicate for the deceased after the third.
There is no fixed supplication. However, if he supplicates using a du‘ā’ which has been
transmitted from the Prophet , it is better and more readily accepted.
From amongst these is the du‘ā’ which ‘Awf ibn Malik  learnt from the Prophet :

text_raw:
The most entitled person to lead the prayer for the deceased
The ruler is most entitled to lead the janāzah prayer, then his deputy, then the Q̣āḍi
(judge), then the Imam of the locality then the heir.
The most entitled person may permit someone else to lead the prayers. If another
person (besides the one who is most entitled) leads the janāzah prayer, the most
entitled person may repeat the prayer if he wishes. However, those individuals who
have already offered the prayer with the other person may not repeat their prayers
with him.
The individual who has the right of going forward to lead the janāzah prayer
(mentioned above) has more right than the person regarding whom the dying person
had made a request for, that he lead his prayers after his death, according to the
opinion upon which the fatwa is given.
If the body has been buried without offering janāzah ṣalāh the prayers will be offered
at his grave- even if the body hadn’t been bathed- so long as it hasn’t decomposed.
If there are many dead bodies it is better to offer separate prayers for each one of them.
The noblest will be first then the next in nobility and so on and so forth.
If there are many bodies and one prayer is being offered (for all of them), all the bodies
will be placed in a long line in the direction of the q̣iblah in a manner that the chest of
everybody is in front of the Imam. The order will be taken into consideration when
placing the bodies; the men will be placed closest to the Imam, then the children, then
the hermaphrodites and finally the females.
If many bodies are being placed in a single grave they will be placed in the opposite
sequence.
The person who finds the Imam between two takbīrs will not join him immediately.
Rather he will wait for the Imam to make takbīr and then join him. He will coincide
with the Imam in his supplication. Thereafter he will complete what he missed before
the bier is lifted.
An individual who was present at the takbīr al-taḥrīmah of the Imam will not wait for
the Imam to make takbīr (before joining him).69
Whoever comes after the fourth takbīr prior to the salām has missed the janāzah
prayer according to the sound position.
It is disliked to offer the janāzah prayers in a masjid in which congregational prayers
are held whilst the corpse is in it, or the corpse is outside but some people are in the
masjid, according to the preferred opinion.

text_raw:
The most entitled person to lead the prayer for the deceased
bath and janāzah prayers will be offered upon him.
If the child does not make a sound (i.e. show signs of life) he will be given a bath
according to the preferred opinion, and wrapped in a cloth and buried without
offering janāzah prayers upon him.
The same ruling applies to a child who has been captured with one of his parents,
unless:
 One of his parents become Muslim,
 He himself becomes Muslim,
 Or neither of his parents were captured with him (i.e. he was captured alone).70
If a deceased non-Muslim has a Muslim relative, he (the Muslim relative) will bathe
him as washing an impure rag and then enshroud him in a cloth and fling him into a
ditch, or pass him to his co-religionists.
The janāzah ṣalāh will not be offered for:
 A rebel,
 A highway robber killed in a confrontation,
69 If an individual is present at the time of takbīr at taḥrīmah but due to some reason fails to join the Imam, he will not
have to wait for the Imam to make another takbīr before joining in. Rather he may join in whenever he is ready, even if it
is between two takbīrs. (Translator)
70 In all these scenarios the child will be dealt with as a Muslim child is dealt with: his janāzah ṣalāh will be offered. (ibid.)
 A murderer who kills by strangling his victim after misleading them into a trap
before killing them,
 An armed trouble-maker by night in the city
 And an individual who has been killed in nationalist/sectarian violence
though they will be bathed.
A person who has committed suicide will be bathed and his janāzah prayers will be
offered.
The janāzah prayers will not be offered for a person who intentionally murders one of
his parents.

text_raw:
Lifting and burying the bier
It is sunnah to have four men to lift the bier and each person should carry it for forty
steps.
 An individual will start by carrying the front right side of the coffin upon his
right shoulder. The right side of the coffin is that side of the coffin which is on
the left of the carrier (if he stands with his back to the coffin).
 Then the back right side of the coffin upon his right shoulder.
 Then the front left side of the coffin upon his left shoulder.
 And finally the back left side of the coffin upon his left shoulder.
It is preferable to walk fast with the coffin without running which results in the body
being jostled.
To walk behind the bier is better than walking in front of it, just as farḍ ṣalāh is better
in comparison to nafl ṣalāh.
It is makrūh to recite dhikr aloud and to sit before putting down the bier.
The grave will be dug a depth of half ones height or to chest-height. If it is dug deeper
it is better.
A laḥd style grave will be dug, not a shiq̣q̣ style grave, unless in soft land.
The body will be entered into the grave from the q̣iblah side. The person placing the
body will say:

In the name of Allāh  and in accordance to the creed of the Prophet of Allāh .
The body will be made to face the q̣iblah on his right side. The knots will be
unfastened and unbaked bricks and bamboo will be levelled upon him. It is disliked to
use baked bricks and timber.
The female’s grave will be covered with a cloth (when lowering her body into it), not a
male’s grave.
Soil will be thrown (to fill up the grave) and the grave will be shaped like a camel’s
hump; it will not be made cuboid.
It is impermissible to construct upon a grave for the purpose of beautifying it and it is
makrūh to construct in order to strengthen the grave after the burial has taken place.
There is nothing wrong with writing upon the grave so the indication (as to who is
buried there) does not disappear and the burial site is not disrespected.
It is makrūh to bury indoors as this is a speciality of the Prophets . It is also makrūh
to bury in tombs.
There is no problem with burying more than one individual in a single grave in dire
circumstances. Each body will be separated from the next with a layer of soil.
Whoever dies on a ship and dry land is far or there is fear of decomposing, the
deceased will be bathed, enshrouded, his janāzah prayers will be offered and he will be
cast into the ocean.

text_raw:
Lifting and burying the bier
It is preferable to bury the deceased where he has died or has been killed. If the body is
moved a distance of a mile or two before burial there is no problem. However, to move
it further than that is disliked.
There is general agreement that it is impermissible to move the body once it has
already been buried, unless the burial site is usurped land, or the land has been taken
over on the basis of pre-emption.
If the deceased has been buried in a grave which was dug for someone else, he will be
liable to pay the expenses of having the grave dug71 but will not be taken out of it.
The grave may be re-dug (after the deceased has been buried)
 Due to some item falling in it
 Or if the shroud was usurped
 Or wealth/treasure was buried with the deceased.
The grave will not be re-dug due to not facing the deceased towards the q̣iblah, or due
to placing him on his left. And Allāh  knows best.

text_raw:
Visiting Graves
It is preferable for both males and females to visit graves according to the soundest
view. It is mustaḥab to recite Sūrah Yā Sīn, as it has been narrated: “Whomsoever
enters the graveyard and recites Yā Sīn, Allāh will lighten their (the inhabitants of the
graves) punishments for that day, and he (the reciter) will receive a reward equal to the
number of the inhabitants of the grave.”
It is not makrūh to sit on the grave for recitation according to the preferred opinion.
It is, however, makrūh to
 Sit on the grave for any other purpose besides recitation
 To trample it
 To sleep upon it
 To relieve oneself on it
 To uproot grass and trees from the graveyard.
There is no harm in uprooting dry grass and trees.

text_raw:
Rulings pertaining to a martyr
A martyr is he who has been killed and has died due to his appointed lifespan elapsing
according to us, i.e. the Ahl al-Sunnah.
71 The expenses will be paid from the deceased’s wealth which he has left behind. (al-Iṣbāḥ, page 322)
Definition of a martyr
A martyr is someone who has been killed by:
 Ahl al-ḥarb (enemy forces) ,
 Rebels,
 Highway robbers,
 Thieves who kill him in his house, even if with a heavy object,
 Or the individual is found dead in a battlefield with signs (which show that he
has been killed)
 Or if he is unrightfully killed by a Muslim intentionally with a sharp object
provided the dead person is a mature Muslim who is not in the state of ḥaiḍ, nifās or
janābah, and has not benefited from the world after the battle ceased.
The martyr will be enshrouded with his blood in the clothes he is wearing and his
janāzah ṣalāh will be offered without bathing him.
He will be stripped of those items of clothing which are not suitable for a shroud like
fur coats, extra layers (of clothing), weapons and armour.
Clothing may be added or partly removed (in order to comply with the sunnah kafn),
but it is makrūh to strip him of all his clothing.
The deceased will be bathed if he/she has died:
 As a child,
 In the state of insanity,
 In the state of ḥaiḍ,
 In the state of nifās,
 In the state of janābah,
 Or if the deceased benefitted from the world after the battle ceased by:
o Eating,
o Drinking,
o Sleeping,
o Seeking medical treatment,
o Or a full ṣalāh time passes whilst he is conscious,
o Or he is removed from the battlefield unless he is moved for the fear of
being trampled on,
o Or he makes a will,
o Or buys or sells
o Or speaks a considerable amount.
If the above-mentioned things take place before the battle ceases the dying person will
not be considered to have benefited from the world (and therefore will still be counted
a martyr).
A person who is found dead in a city and it is not known whether he was kill unjustly
with sharp object or killed as a punishment or on the basis of q̣iṣāṣ (retaliation), will be
bathed and his janāzah ṣalāh will be offered.

text_raw:
The Book of Fasting
The technical meaning of fasting
Fasting is to abstain from entering anything into the stomach - intentionally or
unintentionally - and that which holds the ruling of a stomach (e.g. brain), and from
fulfilling lustful desires with a suitable72 intention.
The cause of Ramaḍān to become wājib
It becomes wājib for one to fast in Ramaḍān when he witnesses a part of it, and every
day of Ramaḍān will be a cause to fast for that day.
The ruling of fasting, and conditions of its compulsion
It is farḍ to keep the fasts of Ramaḍān (whether during Ramaḍān or after) for the one
in whom these four things are all found:
1. Islām
2. Sanity
3. Maturity
4. Knowledge of it being wājib for a person who has embraced Islām in a Dar al-
Ḥarb or
5. By a person being in a Dār al-Islām
Conditions which necessitate its fulfilment
It is incumbent for a person to fast if:
1. He is free from any illness
2. A woman is not in ḥaiḍ -
3. nor nifās
4. He/she is a resident
72A suitable intention is an intention which discerns an action between a form of worship and a habit. (al-Iṣbāḥ, page
326)
Conditions which validate its fulfilment
There are three conditions for a person’s fasting to be correct:
1. Intention
2. To be free from those things with which fasting is impermissible, like ḥaiḍ and
nifās
3. To be free from those things which nullify the fast
To be free from major impurity (janābah) is not a condition.
Its rukn
The rukn of fasting is to abstain from fulfilling the desires of the stomach, private
parts, or to perform any other action which holds the same ruling.
Its outcome
The outcome of fasting is that a wājib will lapse from one’s responsibility, and he will
attain reward in The Hereafter, and Allāh  knows best.

bab: Types of fasts, and an explanation of every type
text_raw:
Types of fasts, and an explanation of every type
There are 6 types of fasts:
1. Farḍ
2. Wājib
3. Sunnah
4. Mandūb
5. Nafl
6. Makrūh
The following fasts come under the category of farḍ:
 The fasting of Ramaḍān (be it in Ramaḍān or after)
 Fasting of kaffārah (expiation)
 And the fasting of nadhr (fulfilment of a vow), according to the most apparent
view.
As for wājib, it is to fulfil those nafl fasts which had been nullified.
As for sunnah, it is to keep fast on the 9th and 10th of Muḥarram.
The following fasts come under the category of mandūb:
 The fasting of 3 days every month; it is preferable they be from amongst the
Ayyām al-Bīḍ, which are the 13th, 14th and 15th
 Fasting on Mondays and Thursdays
 Fasting for 6 days in Shawwal. Some say that to keep them consecutively is
preferable, whilst others have opined their preference to keep them separately.
 Every fast which the sunnah has promised reward for, like the fasting of
Prophet Dāwūd . He would fast on alternate days, and this form of fasting is
the best and most loved by Allāh .
As for nafl, it is those fasts which are not mentioned in the aforementioned categories
of fasting, and its disapproval is not established.
Makrūh fasts are of two types:
 Makrūh Tanzīhī: To fast on the 10th of Muharram only (without fasting on the
9th or 11th as well).
 Makrūh Taḥrīmī: To fast on Eid al-Fiṭr, Eid al-Aḍḥā, or the Days of Tashrīq̣.
It is also Makrūh to fast only on:
 Fridays,
 Saturdays,
 The Iranian New Year’s Day73,
 And the Iranian Festival Day74 -
unless that day complies with one’s habit of fasting.
Ṣawm al-Wiṣāl is makrūh, even though it may be for only two days. This is to continue
fasting, even after sunset, so that the fast of the previous day connects with the fast of
the following day. To fast continuously throughout one’s life is also makrūh.

bab: Chapter on those fasts which require a specified intention from the night, and those that do not
text_raw:
Chapter on those fasts which require a specified intention from the night,
and those that do not
Those fasts that do not require a specific intention from the night
These are:
 Fasts of Ramaḍān,
 Fasting to fulfil a vow for which the date has been specified (nadhr mu‘ayyan)
 And nafl fasts.
Therefore, if the intention for any of these fasts was made at any time from the night to
just before midday, the fast will be valid, according to the soundest view. ‘Midday’ in
this context refers to the midpoint between subḥ ṣādiq̣ and sunset, referred to as al-
ḍaḥwat al-kubrā75.
The fast will also be valid if the intention was left unspecified or if the intention for a
nafl fast was made. This will also be the case if the one who has intended is a musāfir
or an ill person according to the soundest view.
Fasting in Ramaḍān will be valid with the intention of another wājib fast for a person
who is a resident and physically well. This is in contrast to a musāfir, who will fast for
whatever wājib fast he intends. However, there is a difference of opinion with regards
to preference for the ill person when he intends for a different wājib fast during
Ramaḍān.
A nadhr mu‘ayyan fast where the date has been specified will not be valid if the
intention of any other wājib fast was made; rather, the intender will fast for whatever
he has intended for.
Those fasts that require a specific intention from the night
These are:
 Q̣aḍā’ of Ramaḍān,
 Q̣aḍā’ of a nafl fast which had been nullified,
75‘Zawāl’ is the term used for midday, which is the midpoint from the time of sunrise to sunset. ‘al-Ḍaḥwat al-Kubra’ is
the term used to identify the midpoint between the beginning of Fajr and sunset. (al-Iṣbāḥ, page 330)
 All categories of expiatory fasts (kaffārah)
 And nadhr muṭlaq̣ – for example, if one were to say ‘If Allāh  cures me of my
illness, I will fast for a day’, and his health improves.

bab: Chapter on those things through which sighting of the hilāl is established, and fasting on the Day of Doubt
text_raw:
Chapter on those things through which sighting of the hilāl is established,
and fasting on the Day of Doubt
With what does Ramaḍān become established
Ramaḍān is initiated through the sighting of the hilāl, or by the passing of 30 days of
Sha‘bān when the hilāl cannot be sighted.
The Day of Doubt and its fast
The Day of Doubt is the day following the 29th of Sha‘bān, where due to a lack of
prospect for sighting the moon, both possibilities (i.e. of Ramaḍān starting or not) are
equal. All types of fasts on that day are makrūh except nafl, where the fasting person
must be firm in his intention between keeping a nafl fast and any other type. If it
becomes apparent that the Day of Doubt was indeed the first of Ramaḍān, then his
fasting of that day will suffice for him (for Ramaḍān), and if he had doubted in his
intention of fasting, his fast will not be counted.
It is makrūh to fast for a day or two at the end of Sha‘bān. Anything more than that is
not makrūh.
On that day, the Mufti will order the people to wait (refrain from eating), and if the
situation is not clarified before the time of making the intention departs, then he will
instruct them to eat.
However, the Mufti himself and the Judge will fast, along with those who can restrain
themselves from wavering in their intention and prevent it from becoming a farḍ.
Ruling of the one who sights the hilāl of Ramaḍān
Whoever testifies alone to the sighting of the hilāl for Ramaḍān or Eid - and it is
rejected - must fast for that day. It will not be permissible for him to break his fast,
although he is certain that he has seen the hilāl of Shawwal. If he does break his fast, he
must keep q̣aḍā’, but no kaffārah will be due upon him, even though he had broken his
fast prior to the rejection of his testimony by the Judge, according to the sound
position.
Establishment of the hilāl when there is an obstruction in the sky
When there is an obstruction in the sky – such as clouds, dust, etc. - preventing the
sighting of the hilāl, then the testimony of a just person - or a person whose status is
unknown - will be accepted, according to the sound position. This is regardless of the
testifier having only one other person of a similar status affirming his testimony, or
whether the testifier is a woman, slave, or a false accuser who had been punished and
has repented for the month of Ramaḍān. There is no need to utter the words of
testimony nor allegation for the testimony to be accepted.

bab: Chapter on those things through which sighting of the hilāl is established, and fasting on the Day of Doubt
text_raw:
Chapter on those things through which sighting of the hilāl is established, and fasting on the Day of Doubt
In the case of the hilāl of fiṭr (Shawwāl), it is necessary for two free men, or one free
man and two free women to utter the words of testimony for it to be accepted, without
any legal proceedings when there is an obstruction in the sky.
Establishment of the hilāl when there is no obstruction in the sky
When there is no obstruction in the sky, it is necessary for a large group of people to
testify to the sighting of the hilāl of Ramaḍān and Fiṭr. The size of the group of people
will be determined according to the opinion of the Imam according to the soundest
view.
If thirty days of Ramaḍān have passed - and the hilāl of Shawwal cannot be seen
despite the sky being clear - and the month had commenced upon the testimony of
one person’s sighting of the hilāl, then breaking fast is not permissible for the people
on that day. There is a difference of opinion whether the fast should be broken (or
not) if the month had commenced upon the sighting of two just people. However,
there is no difference of opinion regarding breaking the fast if there was initially an
obstruction in the sky (preventing the sighting of the hilāl of Ramaḍān), though it was
established upon the testimony of a single person.
The rulings pertaining to the sighting of the hilāl of Eid al-Aḍḥā are the same as Eid al-
Fiṭr.
Establishment of the hilāl for the rest of the months
For the rest of the months, the hilāl must be sighted by two free men or one free man
and two free women who have not been punished for false accusation.
Disparity of regions
When the hilāl is sighted in one region, then according to the ẓāhir al-riwāyah it is
incumbent upon everyone (including the people in the different regions) to
acknowledge the sighting. This is also the selected view of majority of the scholars, and
upon which the fatwa is given.
Sighting the hilāl during the day – whether before or after zawāl time – will not be
considered for that day; rather, its consideration will take effect the following night,
according to the preferred opinion.76

Chapter on those things which do not nullify the fast
There are twenty-four things which do not nullify the fast:
1. Eating something forgetfully
2. Drinking something forgetfully
3. Having intercourse forgetfully
Note: If the person eating or drinking possesses the capability to fast, then he
should be reminded of his fast by someone who notices him eating or drinking.
To not remind him will be considered as makrūh. However, if he doesn’t
possess the capability to fast, then it is preferable not to remind him.
4. Ejaculating by looking at something
5. Ejaculating by pondering over something -
Though he had continuously looked or pondered until he ejaculated.
6. Rubbing oil on the body
7. Applying Kohl, even though he is able to taste it in his throat
8. To have cupping performed
9. Backbiting
10. Merely intending to break the fast (and not actually breaking it)
11. Entering of smoke into the throat involuntarily
12. Involuntarily entering of dust into the throat, albeit from a grain mill

will depend on the hilāl being sighted before or after the Zawāl time. If sighted after, then that day will not be counted (as
the first of Ramaḍān). If, however, it was sighted before Zawāl time, then Ramaḍān would have started from the previous

bab: Chapter on kaffārah, and what absolves it from someone’s liability
text_raw:
Chapter on kaffārah, and what absolves it from one’s liability
What absolves kaffārah
Kaffārah becomes absolved from one’s liability with the occurrence of ḥaiḍ, nifās, or
any such illness which permits the breaking of fast on the day that it had become
obligatory on someone (÷×م اįѲ |Uد). However, the one who has been compelled to travel
after kaffārah had become obligatory will not absolved from its liability, according to
the ẓāhir al-riwāyah.
Explanation of kaffārah
Kaffārah entails the freeing of one slave, even if the slave is not a believer. If one is
unable to do this, then he must fast for two consecutive months, during which there is
no Eid, nor the days of tashrīq̣. If one is unable to do this too, then he must feed sixty
destitute people, providing each one with a filling lunch and supper, or two lunches
(over two days), or two suppers (over two evenings), or a supper and a pre-dawn
meal80. Or, he can give each destitute half a sāԒ of wheat, flour, sawīq̣81, or one sā’ of
dates or barley. Or, if he wishes, he can give the value of any one of the
aforementioned measured foods.
Overlapping of a number of kaffārah
One kaffārah will suffice for a number of offences perpetrated intentionally - such as
intercourse or eating - over a number of days, though they may be (perpetrated) over
two Ramaḍāns. However, it is a prerequisite that one has not already performed one
kaffārah during these perpetrations, according to the sound position. If during these
perpetrations one had already performed a kaffārah, then one kaffārah will not suffice
for him, according to the ẓāhir al-riwāyah.
80It is necessary that the destitute whom he had fed the second time is the same destitute whom he had fed the first time.
If this isn’t the case, then he must feed one of the two parties a second time. It will also suffice to feed one destitute for
sixty days. (al-Iṣbāḥ, page 341)
81Sawīq̣: An Arabian delicacy; a mush made from dates, sugar, and wheat/ barley. (Hans Wehr, page 517)

Chapter on those things which nullify the fast without necessitating
kaffārah
These are fifty seven things:
1. Eating of uncooked rice
2. Or dough
3. Or flour
4. Or a large amount of salt (in one go)
5. Or soil – which is not armany – and which one is not accustomed to eating
6. Or a date seed
7. Or cotton
8. Or paper
9. Or a raw quince
10. Or a raw walnut
11. Swallowing a pebble
12. Or iron
13. Or soil
14. Or a stone
15. Administration of medicine through the anal passage
16. Or the nose
17. Or (directly into) the throat, according to the soundest view
18. Dripping of oil
19. Or water into the ears, according to the soundest view
20. Medicine reaching the inside of the stomach or brain after one applies it to a
head or stomach wound
21. Entering of a raindrop into the throat
22. Or snow – according to the soundest view – and it was unintentionally
swallowed
23. Breaking of fast unintentionally when the water for gargling goes down the
throat
24. Breaking of fast out of compulsion, albeit through intercourse
25. Committing of intercourse by a compelled woman
26. Breaking of fast by a woman – whether married or a slave – out of fear that she
may become ill due to her domestic services
27. Pouring of water by another person into the mouth of a fasting person whilst he
is sleeping
28. Eating intentionally after one had eaten forgetfully, though he may had been
aware of the ḥadīth82 of Rasūlullāh  according to the soundest view
29. Having intercourse intentionally after having it forgetfully
30. Eating (or drinking) after one had intended to fast from the day, and had not
intended anything from the night
31. Beginning the day as a musāfir, but intended to reside in a place (as a muq̣īm),
and thus takes to eating
32. Beginning the day as a muq̣īm, then becomes a traveller (musāfir), and thus
takes to eating
33. Abstaining from eating, drinking, etc. without an intention to fast, nor to break
it
34. Partaking the pre-dawn meal
35. Or having intercourse out of doubt with regards to the starting of Fajr, whilst it
had already started
36. Breaking the fast, assuming the sun had set, whilst it hadn’t
37. Ejaculating, due to having intercourse with a dead body
38. Or intercourse with an animal
39. Or rubbing the male genitalia with someone’s thighs
40. Or on someone’s stomach
41. Or kissing
42. Or fondling
43. Nullifying a fast other than a Ramaḍān fast
44. For a woman to have had performed intercourse with, whilst she was asleep

bab: Chapter on those upon whom it is wājib to abstain from eating, drinking, and intercourse during the day
text_raw:
Chapter on those upon whom it is wājib to abstain from eating, drinking,
and intercourse during the day
It is wājib to abstain for the rest of the day for:
 One who has nullified his fast
 Or has become pure from ḥaiḍ and nifās
83When a person becomes insane for the entire month of Ramaḍān, fasting will not be obligatory on him, nor will he be
obliged to keep q̣aḍā’. However, if he were to recover for even one day, then keeping q̣aḍā’ of all the missed days will be
necessary. If he recovers (after being insane since the beginning of Ramaḍān) at the night of Eid, or after the time of
making intention on the last day of fasting, then he will not be obliged to keep q̣aḍā’. (Thamarat al-Najāh ‘alā Nūr al-
Īḍāḥ, volume 2, page 221)
 Or has reached maturity
 Or has embraced Islam. (For the latter three, the condition of their occurrence
after the beginning of Fajr is necessary)
Note: Q̣aḍā’ is necessary for all except the latter two.

bab: Chapter on things which are makrūh, not makrūh, and mustaḥab for a fasting person
text_raw:
Chapter on things which are makrūh, not makrūh, and mustaḥab for a
fasting person
Things which are makrūh for a fasting person
These are seven things:
1. Tasting
2. Chewing something without a need84
3. Chewing gum
4. Kissing
5. Intimate touching if one cannot ensure himself not to ejaculate or have
intercourse, according to the ẓāhir al-riwāyah.
6. Gathering saliva in the mouth, then swallowing it.
7. Doing an action which he thinks will weaken him, such as phlebotomy
(incision of a vein) and cupping.
Things which are not makrūh for a fasting person:
Nine things are not makrūh:
1. Kissing and intimately touching if one can ensure himself not to ejaculate or
have intercourse
2. Oiling the moustache
3. Applying kohl
4. Performing cupping
5. Or phlebotomy
84This includes a woman who is able to find someone that will chew the food for her child. However, if it isn’t possible,
then there is no problem with her chewing it herself. If the husband is of an angry temperament, it is permissible for the
wife to taste the content of salt in the food, in contrast to a woman whose husband is not of that temperament. Similar is
the case for a slave woman and an employee. There is a difference in opinion with regards to the one who is in fear of
being cheated when he buys an item that can be tasted (i.e. some have opined that it is permissible for him to taste the
item to ensure he is not being cheated, whilst others have opted to differ). (al-Iṣbāḥ, page 348)
6. Using a miswāk towards the end of the day; rather it is a sunnah, just as it is a
sunnah to use it at the beginning of the day, although it is fresh or has been
wetted by water85.
7. Rinsing the mouth and snuffing water through the nose without performing
wuḍū’
8. Having a shower
9. Wrapping a wetted cloth around oneself to cool down, according to the
juristically preferred opinion (¾ Ѭʑ}ȝا)
Things which are mustaḥab for a fasting person:
These are three things:
1. To partake in suḥūr (pre-dawn meal).
2. To delay in the partaking of suḥūr.
3. Hastening for ifṭār (breaking of fast), except on a cloudy day.

text_raw:
Chapter on valid excuses
Excuse of being ill, pregnancy, suckling, extreme hunger, extreme thirst and travelling
It is valid for the following categories of people to not fast:
1. One who fears his illness may worsen or his cure will be delayed.
2. A pregnant,
3. Or a suckling woman, who fears being afflicted by a mental condition, illness or
death upon herself or the child, regardless of whether it is her own child, or her
suckling child.
4. With regards to the fear of the woman, it must be based upon her predominant
apprehension due to experience, or the advice of an expert, just, Muslim doctor
(general fear will not be taken into consideration).
5. One suffering from severe thirst
6. Extreme life threatening hunger, (or being afflicted with a mental condition, or
losing of a sense, etc.)
7. Or a musāfir
85This is to clarify a difference of opinion that exists regarding the usage of Miswāk towards the end of the day, where
some have claimed that it is Makrūh, like Imām Shāfi‘ī . (Ḥāshiyah al-Ṭaḥṭāwī, page 680)
However, if there is no fear of any harm, nor are the majority of the people whom one
is travelling with are not fasting (i.e. most of his companions are fasting), nor do they
have a joint partnership in expenditure, then fasting is more preferable for the
aforementioned people. Hence, if most of the group (whom one is travelling with) are
not fasting, or they are all in a joint partnership in expenditure, then to not fast is
better, as it is in conformance with the rest of the group.
Bequests and q̣aḍā’
It is not wājib for one who has passed away before the termination of his illness or
journey to bequest the compensation (kaffārah) for those fasts he was unable to keep,
as has been previously mentioned.
However, in the state of physical well-being and residency (i.e. when he is not
travelling), he must do q̣aḍā’ to the extent of him remaining in the state of physical
well-being and residency.
There is no condition of performing q̣aḍā’ successively (i.e. one after another). Whilst
performing q̣aḍā’ if the month of Ramaḍān approaches, he will perform the fasts of
Ramaḍān, and continue his q̣aḍā’ afterwards, and there will be no compensation for
this delay.
Fidyah (redemption) for an aged person
It is permissible for an elderly man or woman not to keep fast. However, for every fast,
they must donate a fidyah, which amounts to half a sā’ of wheat or something of its
value.
Ruling for the one who had vowed to fast for eternity and has become weak

text_raw:
Chapter on valid excuses
For the one who had vowed to fast for eternity and has since become frail and weak to
due to his occupation with earning a livelihood should offer fidyah (in place of
fasting). If this too is difficult for him, he must seek forgiveness and pardon from Allāh
When is it not permissible to give fidyah?
If kaffārah has become wājib upon an aged person due to an oath or a killing, and he
does not possess a slave to free, or has not performed any fasts until he became an
aged person, then offering fidyah will not be permissible in this instance, as fasting
here is a replacement for something else.
Permissibility of breaking an optional fast with and without an excuse
According to one narration, it is permissible to break an optional fast without an
excuse. According to the most apparent view, hosting is regarded as a valid excuse for
both the host and the guest. Rather, there is glad tidings for the one who performs this
highly virtuous act86.
When it is incumbent to keep q̣aḍā’ for breaking an optional fast:
For whichever reason a person had broken his optional fast, he must keep q̣aḍā’.
However, for the following five days, he will not be liable to perform q̣aḍā’: the two
days of Eid, and the days of tashrīq̣, according to ẓāhir al-riwāyah. And Allāh 
knows best.
