bab: Chapter on what is necessary to fulfil from vowing to fast and offer ṣalāh
text_raw:
Chapter on what is necessary to fulfil from vowing to fast and offer ṣalāh
When is it necessary to fulfil a vow?
When the following three things are found in a vow together, it will be necessary to
fulfil that vow:
1. A similar act must be wājib87.
2. It must be an al-ԑibādah al-maq̣sūdah.
3. The vowed action itself cannot be wājib.
Therefore, wuḍū’, sajdah al-tilāwah, visiting the sick or vowing to perform wājib
actions will not become incumbent to fulfil as a vow.
However, it will be valid to vow to set slaves free, perform i‘tikāf, offer ṣalāh (that are
not farḍ) and keep fast. Thus, if one undertakes an unconditional vow (nadhr muṭlaq̣)
86It is written in al-Tajnīs wa al-Mazīd: A man had intended to keep an optional fast from the morning, but when he
entered upon a brother’s house, he was requested to break his fast. In this case, there is no problem in breaking his fast
due to the saying of Rasūlullāh : ‘Whoever breaks his fast to fulfil the right of a brother, the reward of keeping fast for a
thousand days will be written for him. When he performs q̣aḍā’ of that fast, the reward of keeping fast for two thousand
days will be written for him.’  (al-Iṣbāḥ, page 353)
87The original condition that determines the validity of a vow is that the mandhūr (vowed item) must not be wājib
(obligatory). However, the original species of that certain act of worship must have been made wājib by Allāh  as an al-
ԑibādah al-maq̣sūdah (a form of worship that had been made obligatory from the onset). (ibid.)
or stipulates a condition of the existence of something for it (nadhr muԑallaq̣), it will be
incumbent for him to fulfil it.
Ruling for the one who vows to fast on an Eid day
It is permissible to vow to fast on Eid day or from the days of tashrīq̣, according to the
preferred opinion. However, it is wājib for him to break the fast and do q̣aḍā’ for it
later on. If he does fast, it will suffice (for the fulfilment of his vow), but with the ruling
of makrūh taḥrīmī.
Things which are and are not taken into consideration when vowing
Specifying a certain time, place, dirham or poor person has been invalidated, so fasting
in the month of Rajab will suffice for the one who had vowed to fast in Sha’bān.
Similarly, offering two rakā’ah in any city will suffice for the one who had vowed to
offer two rakā’ah in Makkah, and donating any dirham to charity will suffice for the
one who had specified a certain dirham to donate.  Likewise, donating to a poor ‘Zayd’

text_raw:
Chapter on I‘tikāf
The shar‘ī meaning:
It (i.e. i‘tikāf) is to reside, with an intention, in such a Masjid where the five daily
prayers are performed in congregation. Thus, performing i‘tikāf in a Masjid where the
five daily prayers are not performed in congregation will not be valid, according to the
preferred opinion. For females, i‘tikāf is performed in the Masjid of their house; this is
the part which has been specified to offer ṣalāh.
Types of i‘tikāf
I‘tikāf is of three types:
1. Wājib, when fulfilling a vow.
2. Sunnah Kifāyah Mu’akkadah in the last ten days of Ramaḍān.
3. Mustaḥab in any other time of the year.
Fasting is only a prerequisite when performing i‘tikāf of a mandhur. The shortest
duration of i‘tikāf one may offer as a nafl is a brief moment, even though it may just be
a walk through the Masjid, according to the juristically preferred opinion (¾ Ѭʑ}ȝا).
Ruling of exiting the Masjid for a mu’takif
A mu’takif is not permitted to exit the Masjid except for the following reasons:
 A need pertaining to the sharī‘ah, like Jumu‘ah
 A need pertaining to nature, like passing urine.
 A dire necessity, like the destruction of the Masjid.
 Removal through compulsion by a tyrant.
 Separation from one’s family.
 Fearing for one’s self or for his luggage from rebels.
In the aforementioned scenarios, he should exit and enter another Masjid as soon as
possible.
Thus, if one exits the Masjid without a valid excuse, then his wājib i‘tikāf will become
void, and any other type of i‘tikāf (sunnah, nafl, etc.) will terminate.
What a mu’takif is permitted to do in the Masjid
It is permissible for a mu’takif to eat, drink, sleep and transact with items of necessity
for himself or his family in the Masjid.
Makrūh acts for a mu’takif in the Masjid
It is makrūh for a mu’takif to
 Bring items of transaction into the Masjid,
 Transact for the sake of business,
 Remain silent (thinking it to be a form of worship),
 Speak something other than good.
Those things which are ḥarām for a mu’takif, and what nullifies the i‘tikāf
It is ḥarām for a mu’takif to have intercourse, or to perpetrate anything which
resembles it. Hence, i‘tikāf becomes nullified by intercourse or ejaculation by anything
related to intercourse.

incumbent upon him. Similarly, vowing to perform i‘tikāf for a few nights

Chapter on I‘tikāf
automatically necessitates the i‘tikāf of its days. Continuity is also incumbent upon
him, although it was not stipulated by him, according to the ẓāhir al-riwāyah. Hence,
vowing to perform i‘tikāf for two days also necessitates the i‘tikāf of two nights. It is
permissible to intend to perform i‘tikāf for only the days without the nights. If one
intends to perform i‘tikāf for a month – intending only the days, or only the nights –
his intention will not be valid; thus he must explicitly specify, exempting either the
days or the nights from the entire month.
Permissibility of i‘tikāf: its status and its ruling
I‘tikāf has been established (i.e. made permissible) from the Q̣urԒān and sunnah. It is
amongst the most noble of actions when performed sincerely for the sake of Allāh .
From its benefits is that one frees his heart from the affairs of the dunyā, surrenders
himself to The Master, maintains his worship in the House of Allāh  and seeks
protection in the Fort of Allāh .
‘Atā’ ibn Abū Ribāḥ  has stated: ‘The example of a mu’takif is of a man who stands
at the door of The Great  seeking for something, saying: ‘
’ i.e. ‘I will
continue to stand here until He forgives me.’
Sheikh Shurunbulālī  states:
And this (i.e. compilation of this book) is that which has been made easy for the lowly
and helpless one, through the help and supervision of The Master, The All-Powerful,
The All-Able. All praise is for Allāh , who has guided us to this, and we would not
have been guided had he not guided us.
May Allāh  shower mercy upon Our Leader, Our Master, Muḥammad , the Seal
of the Prophets, and upon his family, his companions, his progeny, and whoever aids
him and follows him in goodness.
To Allāh  we implore, as beseechers, that he makes this solely for his noble self, a
means of universal benefit, and a cause of substantial reward.

The Book of Zakāh
Its definition and ruling
Zakāh is the transferring of ownership of a specific amount of wealth to a specific
person.
It is Farḍ upon every free Muslim, upon whom the rulings of Sharī‘ah apply, that owns
at least the niṣāb in the form of currency (i.e. gold and silver) – whether it be in the
form of nuggets, jewellery or receptacles. That which reaches the value of the niṣāb (of
either gold or silver) from goods of trade will also necessitate zakāh for its owner -
provided that he is free from any debts and is not in dire need of any basic necessities -
and his wealth falls under the category of ‘nāmī’88, albeit in ruling and not reality.
The condition that necessitates offering of zakāh
For zakāh to be wājib, one complete year89 must pass whilst the owner is in possession
of an original niṣāb.
If any addition is made to the original niṣāb during the course of the year, it will be
added to its genus for which zakāh will be given upon the completion of one year of
the original niṣāb. This is regardless whether this addition had been made either
through trade, inheritance or any other form (gifts, charity, etc.).
If a person possessing the niṣāb delays in giving zakāh by many years, it is permissible.
A condition for validating the fulfilment of zakāh
For zakāh to be valid, an intention at the time of its fulfilment must be made. This can
be made whilst one is giving it to the poor, or (can be made) by his representative -
whom he has given the liability of fulfilling his zakāh – or when he extracts the
amount for zakāh from his wealth and keeps it to one side (though this is not at the
time of fulfilment; hence, it is referred to as muq̣āranah ḥukmī). Similarly, if one had
given zakāh without an intention, and then makes an intention whilst the wealth is in
the possession of the poor person, his fulfilment will be valid.
88‘Nāmī’ is generally referred in Sharī’ah to that wealth which has the tendency to grow, either through sexual
reproduction (e.g. slaves), asexual reproduction (e.g. crops, plants, etc.) or profit (goods of trade). This is also known as
nāmī ḥaq̣īq̣ī. Any other form of wealth which does not grow in a literal sense, but possesses the possibility of increasing
in value - like gold and silver - is known as nāmī taq̣dīrī/ḥukmī. This is the type of wealth indicated to in the text as ‘in
ruling’. (al-Iṣbāḥ, page 361, and Mu‘jam Lughāt al-Fuq̣ahā’, page 397)

It is not necessary for the poor person to know that the wealth given to him is zakāh;
thus, if one offers him the wealth by means of a gift or loan – whilst intending it to be

If one donates his entire wealth in charity, and had not intended for zakāh, his liability
of zakāh will lapse.
Zakāh of debts
There are three types of zakāh for debts: Q̣awī, Wasaṭ and Da‘īf.
The Q̣awī debt
Q̣awī refers to the wealth that one is owed due to a loan, or from a buyer in a business
transaction who has taken the item into possession (and has not yet paid for it). This is
compulsory upon the creditor/seller who confesses to it - though he may be bankrupt
– and the debtor/buyer who rejects it after evidence has been established against him.
Its ruling
The ruling for a q̣awī loan entails that zakāh must be given for what was due from the
past.90The creditor/seller will delay in offering zakāh until forty dirhams comes into
his possession, for which he will be liable to pay one dirham in zakāh. This is because
zakāh is disregarded for whatever is less than 20% of the niṣāb.91 Similarly, zakāh will
be offered on whatever exceeds forty dirhams in this proportion.92
The Mutawassiṭ debt
Wasaṭ refers to the debt which a seller is owed from the sale of an item which was not
sold for a business purpose. For example: the selling of a cloth, slave (for service), or a
house (for accommodation).
90Once the debt has been fulfilled, it is the liability of the creditor to offer zakāh from the debt for what had reached the

The Book of Zakāh
most authentic view.
The Da‘īf debt
Da‘īf is a debt owed in exchange for something that is not wealth; such as dowry, will,
payment for khula‘, compensation for an intentional killing, blood money, payment of
emancipation and labour (for a slave).
Its ruling
Zakāh is not obligatory until it comes into the creditor’s possession and one year
passes, according to Imam Abū Ḥanīfah . Imam Ṣāḥibayn  has obligated that
zakāh is wājib for all three types of debts according to their proportions, regardless of
the quantity.
Zakāh on debt that is deemed as uncollectible
When a debt that had seemed uncollectible comes into the possession of the creditor,
he is not liable to offer zakāh for the previous years. This can include:
 A runaway slave,
 Or a lost slave, when both were bought for business purposes.
 Usurped wealth upon which the owner had no evidence,
 Wealth that had fallen into the sea,
 Or buried in the desert,
 Or in a large house, the whereabouts of which the owner had forgotten,
 Wealth confiscated oppressively (by a tyrant),
 Or wealth deposited in the hands of an unknown person,
 Or a loan for which the creditor had no evidence.
Various rulings
Releasing a poor person from debt with the intention of zakāh will not suffice as
zakāh. It is permissible to offer items of length, measure and weight as zakāh in place
of gold and silver, provided that their value reaches the niṣāb. However, when gold
and silver are offered as zakāh, their weight, rather than their value, will be taken into
account, just as the zakāh had become obligated upon them due to their weight, rather
than their value. Transactional goods may be added to gold and silver, whilst the value
of gold may be added to silver (in order to complete the niṣāb). Any deficiency
incurred in the niṣāb during the course of a year will not be considered if the niṣāb was
met during the beginning and end. Thus, if an item is owned for business purposes,
the value of which does not reach the niṣāb, and the owner does not possess anything
else besides it, then zakāh will not be obligatory upon it for that year if its value reaches
the niṣāb at the end of the year.
The niṣāb of gold and silver
The niṣāb of gold is twenty mithq̣āls. The niṣāb of silver is two hundred dirhams, from
which every twenty dirhams are equivalent to seven mithq̣āls in weight. Whatever
exceeds the niṣāb and reaches a fifth, zakāh will be offered upon it with due

The Book of Zakāh
proportion.93 Any item which contains a mixture of gold/silver and impurity – if the
content of gold/silver is more than the impurity, it will be regarded as pure.
Zakāh of gems and pearls
There is no zakāh for gems and pearls unless they are owned for business purposes,
like all other goods of trade.
93This is according to Imam Abū Ḥanīfah . Thus, zakāh will not be offered on anything that exceeds two hundred
dirhams until it reaches two hundred and forty dirhams. Once the amount reaches two hundred and forty dirhams, then
twenty one dirhams will be due for zakāh. This is because forty dirhams is a fifth of the entire niṣāb, and the proportion
for fulfilment will increase by every fifth of the niṣāb. According to Imam Ṣāḥibayn , zakāh will be offered in
proportion to whatever the amount is, regardless of whether a fifth has been reached or not. (al-Iṣbāḥ, page 366)
Miscellaneous
If an entire year passes upon items of measure and weight that are part of goods (for
trade), during which their prices fluctuate (i.e. become more expensive or cheap), then
there are two ways to offer zakāh: if 2.5% is extracted from the item itself, it will
suffice; and if zakāh is offered from their value, then according to Imam Abū Ḥanīfah
, its value on the day zakāh became obligatory (i.e. at the completion of one year)
will be considered. However, Imam Ṣāḥibayn  have opted to consider its value on
the day zakāh is given. A person who is careless (in offering zakāh) – but not
necessarily destructive in his wealth – will not be liable (for the destruction of his
wealth) if he does not offer zakāh upon the completion of a year without an excuse.
This is because the destruction of the entire wealth after the passing of a year (i.e. after
it has become obligatory) drops the obligation of zakāh, and the destruction of a
portion of the wealth decreases the obligated amount proportionally. The destroyed
wealth will firstly be averted towards the forgiven amount; if it does not succeed the
forgiven amount, then the original obligation will stand in its place94.
Zakāh cannot be taken forcefully or from the inheritance of a deceased person unless
he had bequeathed for it. Only then, it will be offered from a third of his inheritance.
Imam Abū Yūsuf  has permitted the use of ploys to evade the compulsion of zakāh,
whereas Imam Muḥammad  has disliked the use of ploys.

text_raw:
Recipients of zakāh
Recipients of zakāh
1. The poor person: one who does not possess anything that reaches a niṣāb of
zakāh, nor anything equivalent in value, though he may be physically fit and
earning salary.
2. The destitute i.e. one who does not possess anything,
3.  The contracted slave,
94 For example, if a person possessed 239 dirhams, zakāh will be obligatory upon the 200 dirhams, and the extra 39
dirhams will be regarded as ‘the forgiven amount’. Thus, if the wealth destroyed amounted to 39 dirhams, then the
original zakāh on the 200 dirhams (i.e. 5 dirhams) will still stand. However, if the wealth destroyed exceeded 39 dirhams,
then the zakāh will no longer be obligatory, since the original niṣāb has been affected. This is according to the view of
Imam Abū Ḥanīfah . (al-Iṣbāḥ, page 367)
4. The debtor who does not own anything that reaches a niṣāb or its equivalent in
value in excess to his debt.
5. The one who yearns to strive in the path of Allah  – either he is unable to
fight or unable to perform pilgrimage (due to a lack of necessities).
6. The traveller: one who possesses wealth in his homeland, but does not have
anything with him (in the journey).
7. The zakāh collector: he will be given a sufficient amount for him and for those
who help him.
For the person offering zakāh, he may give it to every single category of the recipients
of zakāh; or he may suffice on giving it to just one category, although the rest may also
be available.
Invalid recipients of zakāh
It is impermissible to give zakāh to:
 A disbeliever,
 A rich person who owns a niṣāb or its equivalent in value from any type of
wealth – which is surplus of his necessities.
 The child of a rich person,
 The Banī Hāshim,

to give zakāh to the Banī Hāshim,
 The offspring or forefathers of the one giving zakāh,
o his wife,
o his slave,
o his contracted slave,
o his slave whom he has partially freed.
It is also similarly impermissible to give zakāh for the shroud of a deceased person, or
to repay his debts, or to buy a slave who will subsequently be freed.
If one offers zakāh to whom he thinks is a valid recipient of zakāh, but it later becomes
apparent that it was not so, then his offering of zakāh will be sufficient for him (i.e. he
will not have to offer zakāh again) unless the recipient was his slave or contracted slave
(for which he will be liable to offer zakāh again).

Recipients of zakāh
It is makrūh to make someone rich (through zakāh). This is when:
 (a poor person is given so much as zakāh that) after paying off his debts, he is
left with an amount which reaches the niṣāb of zakāh,
 Or after distributing to each member of his family an amount less than the
niṣāb (e.g. 190 dirhams), the poor person is still left with an amount which
reaches the niṣāb.
If the amount left over does not reach the niṣāb, then it is not makrūh.
It is mandūb to make someone wealthy enough as not to beg others.
Transferring zakāh to a country other than one’s own
It is makrūh to transfer one’s zakāh after the completion of a year to another place
which is not close, nor are the people there in more need, or more pious, nor it will be
as beneficial as giving education to Muslims.
The best method of offering zakāh is by starting with the nearest of kin, then to one’s
neighbours, then to the people of his area, then to the people in his profession, then to
the people of his city.
Sheikh Abū Ḥafṣ al-Kabīr  has stated: The donations of a man will not be accepted
whilst his kith and kin are needy, until he tends to their needs first.

Chapter on Sadaq̣at al-Fitr
Who is sadaq̣at al-fitr wājib upon?
Sadaq̣at al-Fitr is wājib upon every free Muslim who owns wealth that reaches a niṣāb
of zakāh, or something equivalent to it in value. However, there is no condition of the
completion of a year over the wealth, nor does it have to be for business purposes.
Sadaq̣at al-Fitr becomes wājib at the beginning of Fajr (subḥ al-ṣādiq̣) on the Day of
Eid al-Fitr.  The wealth (which reaches a niṣāb or its equivalent) must be free from
debts, and excess of any dire necessities and family essentials. Family essentials are
according to what is sufficient for a family, rather than what have been set as essentials
by the family. These include his residence, furniture, clothes, horses, armour and
slaves of service.
A person will take out sadaq̣at al-fitr for himself and his young children who are
financially dependent upon him. If they are not financially dependent upon him, then
he will extract it from their wealth.  Sadaq̣at al-Fitr is not wājib upon the grandfather
(to give on behalf of his grandchildren) according to the ẓāhir al-riwāyah. However,
the preferred opinion is that the grandfather will take the father’s position in his
absence (e.g. due to death) or if he is poor. A person will also take sadaq̣at al-fitr out
for his slaves who serve him, his mudabbar slave, and the mother of his child, although
they are all disbelievers.
A person will not take out sadaq̣at al-fitr for his contracted slave, his elderly children,
his wife, his shared slave, the runaway slave until after he returns, his usurped slave,
and his captured slave.
Amount of sadaq̣at al-fitr
The amount for sadaq̣at al-fitr is half a ṣā‘ of wheat, flour or sawīq̣, or one ṣā‘ of dates,
raisins, or barley. One ṣā‘ is equivalent to eight Iranian ritls.
It is also permissible to give the equivalent in value; rather, this is better if one finds a
poor person who is need of the money, as it will help him to fulfil his needs quicker
(than giving food). However, if it is a time when food is scarce (e.g. drought, famine,
etc.), then giving wheat or barley is better than giving dirhams.
Time of compulsion
Sadaq̣at al-Fitr becomes wājib from the beginning of Fajr time on the Day of Eid al-
Fitr. Thus, it is not wājib upon the one who passes away, becomes afflicted with
poverty before this time, embraces Islam, becomes rich or is born after it.
It is preferable that it be extracted before one goes to offer Eid prayer.  The giving of

The Book of Hajj
Its technical meaning and time
The technical meaning of Hajj is to visit specified places and perform specific rituals
during the months of Hajj. The months of Hajj are Shawwal, Dhū al-Q̣a‘dah and Dhū
al-Ḥijjah.
Its manner of compulsion
According to the most authentic view, Hajj is farḍ once in one’s lifetime, at the first
instance.
Conditions for Hajj to become compulsory
There are eight conditions for Hajj to become compulsory according to the most
authentic view:
1. Islam,
2. Sanity,
3. Maturity,
4. Being free,
5. Time,
6. Being able to afford provisions for the journey without being extravagant or
miserly, though one lives in Makkah.
7. For a person living outside Makkah: being able to afford his own transport or a
part of a mount – either through owning it or hiring it. Merely borrowing it or
being given it free of charge will not be considered. For those living around
Makkah, it is stipulated for them to be able to walk on foot without any
difficulty. If unable to do so, then they must be able to afford a mount.
The cost (for transport/mount) must be in excess of one’s own and his family’s
expenditure until he returns. This also includes necessities which one cannot
do without, like spending on his house, furniture, heating utensils and
fulfilment of debts.
8. Knowing of the obligation of Hajj for one who becomes Muslim in a Dār al-
Ḥarb, or by merely being in a Dār al-Islam.
Conditions that necessitate its fulfilment
There are five conditions – according to the most authentic opinion - which
necessitate the fulfilment of Hajj:
1. Healthiness of body,
2. Removal of any susceptible restriction which prevents going to Hajj,
3. Safe path,
4. Not being in a waiting period (of a divorce or death),
5. For a woman to travel (that distance wherein one becomes a musāfir) with a
maḥram (unmarriageable kin – either due to suckling or marriage) who is a
Muslim (or a dhimmī), trustworthy, sane, mature (or adolescent), or her
husband.
The predominant safety of the journey – be it through land or sea – is taken into
consideration according to the juristically preferred opinion.
Conditions that validate its fulfilment
For a free person, there are four things which validate his fulfilment of Hajj:
1. Iḥrām,
2. Islam,
3. Performing wuq̣ūf95 in the state of iḥrām in ‘Arafah for a moment – at any time
from the zawāl time of 9th Dhū al-Ḥijjah until the beginning of Fajr on the day
of naḥr (10th Dhū al-Ḥijjah), with the condition of not having performed

5. To recite the talbiyah frequently after donning the iḥrām, with a raised voice,

Chapter on how to perform the rituals of Hajj
When one intends to begin the pilgrimage of Hajj, he should don the iḥrām from one
of the mīq̣āt, like Rābigh97. He will then perform ghusl or wuḍū, though ghusl is better
for cleanliness. Thus, a woman in ḥaiḍ or nifās will perform ghusl if it doesn’t cause
her difficulty.
It is mustaḥab for one to be completely pure, which includes:
 Cutting the nails,
 Trimming the moustache,
 Removing hair from the armpits –
 And pubic regions,
 Having intercourse
 And applying oil, though it be fragranced.
A man will don an izār and a ridā’, which may be new or washed, although it is better
if they are both new and white. He should not button the iḥrām, nor tie a knot, nor
hold it together with a needle/toothpick. It is makrūh to do so, though he will not be
held accountable.
Apply fragrance (O’ pilgrim98) and offer two rakā’ah ṣalāh. Then recite:

Chapter on how to perform the rituals of Hajj
 Hunting land animals
 Indicating towards them
 Guiding towards them
 Wearing stitched clothing, the turban, and socks
 Covering the head and face
 Applying fragrance
 Removing hair from the head, or anywhere else
It is permissible to perform ghusl and seek shade from a tent, a camel-borne litter, or
anything else. It is also permissible to tie a bag around ones waist.
Recite the talbiyah excessively whenever you offer ṣalāh, or climb a hill, or descend
into a valley, or meet a group of riders, and before daybreak, with a loud voice, without
as much exertion as to cause harm to yourself.
99 This is the wording of the talbiyah as it has appeared in Nūr al-Īḍāḥ, alongside its commentaries. However, its wording
differs in the original hadith:

Talbiyah, #1549, volume 4, page 434)
When you reach Makkah, it is preferable to perform ghusl, and enter it though Bāb al-
Mu‘allāh. Thus – out of reverence – you are facing the door of the Ka‘bah when
entering.
It is preferable to recite the talbiyah whilst entering until you reach Bab al-Salām. Then
enter Masjid al-Ḥaram with modesty, humility, reciting the talbiyah, and being
mindful of the magnificence of the place. Enter whilst reciting takbīr, the kalimah, and
sending salutations upon Rasūlullāh . Be considerate of others in a crowd, and do
du‘ā’ for whatever you desire, for verily it is readily accepted at the sight of the
esteemed house.
Thereafter, face the Black Stone whilst reciting takbīr and the kalimah, raise your
hands as you would in ṣalāh, and place them upon the Stone. Next, kiss it without
making any noise. If one is unable to do so without causing harm to another, he
should leave it and rub the stone with something (e.g. a piece of cloth) which he can
kiss thereafter. Or, he may salute the Stone from a distance whilst reciting takbīr, the
kalimah, praising Allah  and sending salutations upon the Prophet .
Subsequently, turn right towards the area of the Ka‘bah which is adjacent to its door,
and perform ṭawāf in the state of iḍṭibā’. Iḍṭibā’ is to: To wrap the ridā’ (upper cloth)
underneath the right armpit and drape both ends over the left shoulder. You must
perform seven circuits, supplicating for whatever you desire therein. Perform ṭawāf
behind the Ḥaṭīm100.
If you intend to perfom sa’y after ṭawāf, you must perform the raml in your first three

Chapter on how to perform the rituals of Hajj
circuits of ṭawāf. The raml is to walk swiftly whilst moving the shoulders, like a proud
soldier would move in between the ranks, yearning to fight the enemy. If the area
around him is crowded with people, he should stop101. If he then finds a gap, he must
perform raml which is necessary for him. He will stop so that he may perform the raml
according to the Sunnah method. This is in contrast to kissing the Black Stone,
wherein there is an alternative – which is to salute it from a distance.
100 The Ḥaṭīm has three names: 1) Ḥaṭīm, 2) Ḥaẓīrah and 3) Ḥijr. This is the name of the area attached to the north-
western side of the Ka’bah. (al-Iṣbāḥ, page 389)
101 The author  has mentioned to stop during crowded times and not move forward unless there is space for one to
perform raml since there is no alternative for raml. This is in contrast to kissing the Black Stone, wherein one may salute
it from afar. However in current times, the crowd rarely disperses during the Hajj season, thus it is best to continue the
ṭawāf at one’s own pace, and perform raml whenever possible (within the first three circuits). (Thamarat al-Najāh,
volume 2, page 357)
He should kiss/salute the Black stone whenever he passes it, and complete his ṭawāf
with it (i.e. kissing/saluting the Black Stone), and performing two rakā’ah ṣalāh at the
Maq̣ām Ibrahim , or wherever it’s easy for him within the Masjid. He will then
return and kiss/salute the Black Stone, and this (complete ritual) is known as ṭawāf al-
q̣udūm, which is sunnah for an outsider.
Then make your way to Ṣafā and climb it until you are able to view the Ka‘bah. Face it
(i.e. the Ka‘bah), reciting takbīr, the kalimah, the talbiyah, sending salutations upon
the Prophet , and supplicating to Allah  with your hands spread out and raised.
Then descend towards Marwah with ease until you102 reach the trough of the valley.
From thereon, walk swiftly between the al-Mīlayn al-Akhḍarayn (the two green
pillars). Once you have crossed the trough of the valley, walk with ease until you reach
Marwah, which you should climb, and do as you had at Ṣafā; face the Ka‘bah whilst
reciting the takbīr, the kalimah, the talbiyah, sending salutations upon the Prophet ,
and supplicating to Allah  with your hands spread out towards the sky. This is one
circuit.
Then return to Ṣafā, and when you reach the Two Green Pillars, walk swiftly, then
continue at ease until you reach Marwah. Climb it and do as you had done in the first

You will perform seven circuits, starting with Ṣafā and finishing at Marwah, whilst

He103 will then stay in Makkah in the state of iḥrām, and perform ṭawāf whenever the
opportunity arises, and this is better than performing nafl ṣalāh for the outsider.
Once he offers Fajr ṣalāh on the eighth of Dhū al-Ḥijjah, he should prepare to travel to
Minā. He will set off for Minā after sunrise. It is mustaḥab to offer Ẓuhr ṣalāh at Minā.
He shouldn’t stop reciting the talbiyah at any time except during ṭawāf.  He will stay in
Minā until he offers Fajr (on the ninth of Dhū al-Ḥijjah) in darkness, and camp near
Masjid al-Khayf. After sunrise, he will set off for ‘Arafah, and encamp there. Once the
sun has passed its peak (i.e. Ẓuhr time has started), he will offer Ẓuhr and ‘Aṣr ṣalāh
with the Imam A‘ẓam or his representative in Masjid Namirah. This will take place

sitting.

taken not to do what the ignorant ones do; travelling at speed, causing the masses to

those passing by. There, he will offer Maghrib and ‘Ishā’ ṣalāh with one adhān and one
iq̣āmah. If he performs nafl ṣalāh, or busies himself in something else in between the

It is a Sunnah to spend the night in Muzdalifah.

If one wishes to hasten in returning to Makkah he may do so before sunset. It is
makrūh to remain in Minā till sunset (then set off for Makkah), though nothing will be
due from him.
If the time for Fajr begins on the fourth day whilst he is still in Minā, it will be
mandatory for him to perform ramy. It is permissible to perform it before zawāl,
although it is better after. However, it is makrūh to perform it before sunrise.
106 A mufrid is one who enters into the state of iḥrām solely to perform Hajj (not ‘umrah). (al-Majmūԑah lil Q̣awā‘id al-
Fiq̣hiyyah, page 292)
That ramy after which another ramy is to be performed should be performed on foot,
so one may supplicate afterwards. If another ramy is not to be performed after, then it
should be performed mounted so one may set out thereafter without supplicating. It is
makrūh to spend the night in any other place apart from Minā during the nights of
ramy107.
Thereafter, when one sets out for Makkah, he should alight at Muḥaṣṣab for a while,
then enter Makkah. He will then perform ṭawāf of the Ka‘bah in seven circuits without
raml or sa’y - if he had previously performed them. This is called ṭawāf al-wadā‘, also
known as ṭawāf al-ṣadr, and is wājib for everyone except the inhabitants and residents
of Makkah. After the ṭawāf, he should perform two rakā’ah ṣalāh.
Drinking the water of Zamzam
He should then come to the well of Zamzam and drink from its water. He should
extract the water himself if possible, face the Ka‘bah, and drink to his fill, whilst taking
a breath in between each sip. He will cast his gaze on the Ka‘bah with every sip, and
pour some water over his body if possible. If not, he will wipe his face and head with
its water. Whilst drinking, he should intend for whatever he desires. Abdullah bin

bab: Chapter on how to perform the rituals of Hajj
text_raw:
Chapter on how to perform the rituals of Hajj
praising him. He will then approach the Black Stone, continuing to praise Allah ,
reciting the kalimah, glorifying him, reciting takbīr, and asking Allah  for his wants
and needs.
He should observe all exterior and interior methods of mannerisms. The green tile
which lies between the two pillars is not the place where Rasūlullāh  offered prayer.
And that elevated place within the walls of the Ka‘bah which many people have alleged
is the ‘Urwat al-Wuthq̣ā (the firm grip) is an innovated fabrication, which is baseless.
Similar is the case with the peg which is located in the middle of the Ka‘bah, which
they (i.e. the innovators) have labelled as ‘the navel of the world’. According to the
citation of Imam Kamāl al-Dīn bin Humām , some of them expose their private
areas and navel, and places it on the peg. This is the act of a brainless person, not to
speak of one who does not possess any knowledge.
Return of the pilgrim to his family
When one intends to return to his family, it is preferable that he sets out after ṭawāf al-
Wadā‘. He should walk backwards, with his face towards the Ka‘bah, crying, or
attempting to cry. He should express grief over parting with the House, until he exits
the masjid. He should then exit Makkah from Bāb Banī Shayba by the al-Thaniyyah al-
Suflā.
The differences between a man and a woman in the rituals of Hajj
A woman is similar to a man in all the rituals of Hajj except the following:
1. She will not uncover her head.
2. She will dangle something in front of her face (as a veil) beneath which there
should be two dome-like pieces of wood, preventing the veil from touching her
face.
3. She will not raise her voice whilst reciting the talbiyah.
4. She will not perform the raml.
5. She will not walk swiftly during sa’y between the two green pillars; rather, she
will walk with ease throughout the whole sa’y between Ṣafā and Marwah.
6. She will not shave off her hair, but trim it.
7. She may wear stitched clothing.
8. She will not horde with men in trying to kiss the Black Stone.
This is the completion of a Mufrid’s Hajj, which is lower in in virtue to the one of a
Mutamatti‘. And Q̣irān is better (in virtue) than Tamattu‘.

Its definition
To combine Hajj and Umrah in one iḥrām.
Its components
He will say after offering the two rakā’ah ṣalāh for iḥrām:

O Allah! I have indeed intended to perform ‘Umrah and Hajj, so make them easy for

He should then recite the talbiyah. When he enters Makkah, he should begin with the
ṭawāf of Umrah, wherein he performs seven circuits, with the raml in the first three

naḥr (tenth of Dhū al-Ḥijjah) during the months of Hajj, and (fast for) seven days after
completion of Hajj, even though he stays in Makkah after the days of tashrīq̣. It is
permissible to keep these seven fasts separately (i.e. without continuity).

text_raw:
Chapter on Tamattu‘
Its definition
To enter into the state of iḥrām from the mīq̣āt solely with the intention of ‘Umrah.
Its components
He will say after performing the two rakā’ah ṣalāh for iḥrām:
Ѵ ѫʑ© ȭا§¥½« إʏѫ Ѵ أر÷F ا¤uªLة |ûŐه ȹѴ و
O’ Allah! I have indeed intended to perform ‘Umrah, so make it easy for me and accept
it from me.
He should then continuously recite the talbiyah until he enters Makkah. He should
then perform the ṭawāf of ‘Umrah – with the raml in the first three circuits - and stop
reciting the talbiyah at the first ṭawāf. Then, he will pray the two rakā’ah ṣalāh of ṭawāf.
He will then perform the sa’y between Ṣafā and Marwah in seven circuits after
standing at Ṣafā, as has passed before. Thereafter, he should shave or trim his head if
he had not brought a sacrificial animal, and everything has now become permissible
for him, including intercourse. He will continue in this unrestricted state. If he had
brought a sacrificial animal as an offering, he will not become released by completing
his ‘Umrah.
When the day of tarwiyah arrives, he will enter into the state of iḥrām for Hajj from
the Ḥaram, and set out towards Minā. When he performs the ramy on the Jamarah al-
‘Aq̣abah on the day of naḥr, it will be binding upon him to slaughter a sheep or one
seventh of a large animal in sacrifice. If he is unable to do so, he should keep fast for
three days prior to the day of naḥr and seven days after he returns like the Q̣ārin. If he
had not fasted before the arrival of the day of naḥr, slaughtering a sheep will be
specified for him; thus, fasting or giving charity will not suffice for him.

Chapter on ‘Umrah
Its ruling
‘Umrah is a Sunnah, and will be valid if performed at any time throughout the year.
However, it is makrūh to perform ‘Umrah on the days of ‘arafah, naḥr and tashrīq̣.
Its method
He will enter into the state of iḥrām from the Ḥill of Makkah. This is contrary to Hajj,
where a person enters into the state of iḥrām from the Ḥaram. As for the outsider who
had not entered Makkah, he will enter into the state of iḥrām from the mīq̣āt when he
intends for Makkah. He will then perform ṭawāf, sa’y and shave his head. He has now
become released from iḥrām, just as we have explained, with praise for Allah .
Note: The best of all days and staying within the vicinity of Makkah
The best of all days is when the day of ‘arafah coincides with the Day of Jumu’ah. This
(i.e. the Hajj performed then) is better than seventy Hajj performed on a day other
than Jumu’ah. This (virtue) has been narrated by the author of Mi‘rāj al-Dirāyah
(Imam Razīn bin Mu‘āwiyah ) by saying ‘This narration from Rasūlullāh  has
been authenticated108, who has stated:

{i.e. the Hajj performed then} is better than seventy Hajj.

Zayla‘ī  – who is the commentator of Kanz al-Daq̣āԑiq̣ – has also narrated
something similar.

Chapter on Offences
Offences
They are of two types:
1. An offence that violates the conditions of iḥrām,
2. And an offence that is perpetrated against the sanctity of the Ḥaram.
The second type of offence is not only specified with a muḥrim.
Types of offences for a muḥrim
Offences perpetrated by a muḥrim are of a few types:
1. That which necessitates an atonement,
2. That which necessitates giving something in ṣadaq̣ah (charity - which is half a
ṣā‘ of wheat),
3. That which necessitates something less than a ṣadaq̣ah (i.e. half a ṣā‘ of wheat),
4. That which necessitates a cost, like the price of a hunted animal. The price of
the hunted animal will multiply according to the number of hunters in the state
of iḥrām.
The First Type
Those things that necessitate an atonement:
 If a mature muḥrim applies perfume to a limb
 Or he dyes his hair with Henna (mehndi)
 He applies olive oil - or something of the like - on his body
 He wears stitched clothing or keeps his head covered for a full day
 He removes a quarter of all hair from his head
 Or (removes hair from) the place of cupping
 Or from one of his armpits
 Or his pubic region
 Or his neck
 He cuts all his nails (from his hands and feet) in one sitting
 Or he cuts all the nails from one hand or a foot
 He leaves out a wājib from amongst those things that have been mentioned
previously.
The judgement of a just person will be required for the one who trims his moustache.
The Second Type
Those things that necessitate giving half a ṣā‘ of wheat, or its value, in ṣadaq̣ah:
 If he applies perfume to a part of the body which is less than a limb
 He wears stitched clothing or keeps his head covered for less than a day
 He removes less than a quarter of hair from his head
 He cuts a nail (similar is the case with every nail. However, if the amount of
ṣadaq̣ah he has to give exceeds the value of an atonement, then he may decrease
the amount, like the one who has cut five separate nails {i.e. they are not all
from the same hand or foot}.)
 He performs ṭawāf al-q̣udūm or ṭawāf al-Sadr in the state of ritual impurity
(one sheep will be wājib upon him if he had performed the ṭawāf in the state of
major ritual impurity {i.e. janābah})
 He leaves out a circuit (whilst performing ṭawāf)
 Similar is the case for every circuit he leaves out until the minimum number of
circuits which is necessary for the ṭawāf to be valid (i.e. three)
 He leaves out pelting a pebble at one of the Jimār

Chapter on Offences
 Similar is the case for every pebble he leaves out, as long as the total amount of
ṣadaq̣ah he owes does not equate to an atonement, which will become wājib if
one misses out performing ramy for one day. If the total amount of ṣadaq̣ah
equals to an atonement or more, than he may decrease it so he does not end up
giving the value of an atonement.
 He shaves off someone else’s hair
 Or cuts someone else’s nails
The choice between slaughtering, ṣadaq̣ah and fasting
If perfume is applied, or stitched clothing is worn, or the head is shaved due to an
excuse, then the perpetrator will be given a choice between slaughtering an animal,
giving ṣadaq̣ah of 3 ṣā‘ to 6 poor people as charity, and fasting for three days.
The Third Type
That which necessitates giving less than half a ṣā‘ (of wheat) in charity: killing a louse
or locust. He will then give in ṣadaq̣ah whatever he wishes.
The Fourth Type
That which necessitates its value: killing game (hunted animals). Two just persons will
then estimate the value of the animal at its place of killing, or near it. If the value
reaches the cost of a sacrificial animal, then the perpetrator will be given a choice:  he
may either buy it (i.e. the sacrificial animal) and slaughter it, or he may buy food and
donate half a ṣā‘ to each destitute. Or, he may keep fast for the number of days equal to
the number of destitute that can be fed in one day. If any food less than half a ṣā‘
remains, then he should give it in charity or fast for one day in lieu of it.
It will be wājib to pay the value of any harm caused by plucking the wings of the one
who could not fly with them, or by plucking its hair, or cutting a limb which will not
prevent it from protecting itself109.  It will also be wājib to pay the (entire) value of the
animal by cutting its legs, plucking its feathers (that will prevent it from protecting
itself) and breaking its eggs.
A person will not give anything more than one sheep in sacrifice in lieu of killing a
wild animal. If it attacks, then nothing will be due from the killer.
Fasting will not be sufficient for an unrestricted person (i.e. who is not in the state of
iḥrām) who had hunted game in the Ḥaram, or cut its grass, or cut those trees that
grow by themselves, and are not from amongst those which people grow. Rather, (for
these offences) the person will be liable for its value. It is ḥarām to use the grass of the
Ḥaram as pasture, or cut it, except for the idhkhir plant and truffles (Terfeziaceae).

text_raw:
Chapter on those things which do not necessitate a penalty by killing them
There is no liability for killing a crow, kite, scorpion, mouse, snake, a voracious
creature (like a wolf or a lion), mosquito, ant, flea, tick, tortoise and that which is not
classed as game.

Chapter on the sacrificial offering
The sacrificial offering and its types
The least a person can offer as a sacrificial offering is one sheep. This is out of camels,
cows and sheep. Whatever is permissible in the sacrifice of Eid al-Aḍḥā, is also
permissible as a sacrificial offering in Hajj. It is permissible to offer a sheep as an
atonement for every offence except for the one who performs ṭawāf al-ziyārah in the
state of janābah, or has intercourse after performing wuq̣ūf (in ‘Arafah) prior to
shaving the head. For these two offences, one is liable to offer a large animal as an
atonement.
The place and time for the sacrificial offering
The offering from the Q̣ārin and Mutamatti‘ has been specified to the day of naḥr
only. Every offering has been specified to take place inside the Ḥaram, unless it is
optional, or the animal had developed a defect on its way to the place of the offering.
Consequently, it will be slaughtered at its place, and no wealthy person may consume
it. A poor person in the Ḥaram is the same (in ruling) as a poor person outside the
Ḥaram.
Bridling the sacrificial offering
Only a large animal being offered as an optional sacrifice, or by a Q̣ārin or Mutamatti‘
will be bridled.
Matters pertaining to the sacrificial offering
The reins and the saddle of the animal should be given away in charity, and they
should not be given as wage to the slaughterer. It should not be ridden on without a
necessity, nor should it should be milked, unless the place of slaughtering is distant.
(Once it is milked) the milk should be given away as ṣadaq̣ah, and, if the place of
slaughtering is near, its teats should be sprinkled with pure, cold water.
Miscellaneous rulings
If one vows to perform Hajj on foot it will be binding upon him, and he should not
ride a mount until performing ṭawāf al-ziyārah. If he rides a mount prior to that, he
must give an atonement in sacrifice.
It is preferable to walk rather than ride a mount for the one who has the capability to
do so.
May Allah  grant us the tawfīq̣, out of his favour and grace, to return in the best of
states to Hajj through the honour of Our Master, Muḥammad . Āmīn.

The Chapter of visiting The Prophet of Allah 
(In a summarised format, in conformance to the most preferred opinions)
Rasūlullāh’s  exhortation to visit
Since visiting Rasūlullāh  is at the height of those actions which please Allah  and
the best of all mustaḥabbat – rather, it is close to the level of a wājib – Rasūlullāh 
had encouraged it and stressed its importance, saying:
Whoever had the means to, but still did not visit me, has verily turned away from me
He has also said:

My intercession is incumbent upon him who had visited me
He also said:
Whoever visits me after my death, it is as if he had visited me while I was alive.
There are many such aḥādīth on this topic.
The Messenger  is alive in his grave
According to what has been agreed by the research scholars, The Prophet  is alive
and being sustained. He benefits from pleasures and worship (just as we do), except
that he is veiled from those who are inadequate to reach the elevated stages.
A few etiquettes for the visit
Since we have realised that the majority of people are heedless to fulfilling the rights of
this visit and (are heedless to) those inclusive and exclusive aspects which have been
made customary for all visitors, we wish to mention a few rituals – which may be

convey the salutations to him (through the means of an angel; this is when the sender
is far). The virtues pertaining to this are too well-known to be mentioned.

should send salutations upon Rasūlullāh , then recite:

In the name of Allah , and upon the religion of Rasūlullāh : {Oh my Lord! Let my
entry be that of truth and honour, let my exit be that of truth and honour, and grant me
from Your Presence an authority to aid me.} O Allah! Send peace upon Our Master,
Muḥammad, and the family of Muḥammad [until the end of the salutation] and
forgive my sins, and open for me the doors of your mercy and grace.
He will then enter the Noble Masjid and offer two rakā’ah ṣalāh of taḥiyyat al-masjid
near the minbar, standing in a manner, so the pillar of the minbar is in line with his
right shoulder since that was the standing spot of The Prophet . That portion of
land which is between His minbar and His grave is a garden from the gardens of
Paradise, just as He had narrated:
My minbar is above the pond of al-Kauthar.
Then110 offer two rakā’ah ṣalāh al-shukr to Allah , as he has granted you the tawfīq̣
and blessed you to reach the sacred place, after which you may supplicate for whatever
you wish.
Greetings upon Rasūlullāh 
Then, set off towards the blessed grave, and stand four arms’ length away from the
blessed tomb with the epitome of respect, with the back towards the q̣iblah and in line
with the head and blessed face of Rasūlullāh . You should be aware that his gaze is
upon you, and he can hear your speech, reply your salām and say Amin to your du‘ā’s.
Thus, say:

Peace be upon you O’ my Master, O’ Messenger of Allah; Peace be upon you, O’ Prophet
of Allah; Peace be upon you O’ Beloved of Allah; Peace be upon you O’ Prophet of
Mercy; Peace be upon you O’ Intercessor of the Ummah; Peace be upon you O’ Leader of
the Messengers; Peace be upon you O’ Seal of the Prophets; Peace be upon you O The
One who is enwrapped; Peace be upon you O’ The One who is enveloped; Peace be upon
You and your pure descendants and family, those whom Allah had rid of all impurity
and wholly purified. May Allah  grant you remuneration from us – the best any
prophet has received from his people and any messenger from his ummah.
I bear testimony that you are the Messenger of Allah; you have duly relayed your
message, fulfilled your trust, guided the Ummah, elucidated the proofs, persevered in the
path of Allah and have laid the foundations for this dīn until death arrived at your door.
May Allah , the Lord of the Worlds, send lasting peace and blessings upon you - and
that place which is venerated by the presence of your pure body – to the extent of the
infinite blessings that were and will be according to the knowledge of Allah .
O’ Messenger of Allah! We are visitors to your sanctuary; ennoble us by permitting us to
stay here, for verily we have arrived from distant lands and places afar. We have
traversed plain and rugged terrains in the hope of your visit, so we may attain success

text_raw:
The Chapter of visiting The Prophet of Allah 
through your intercession, reminiscing over your feats and accomplishments, attempting
to fulfil (a few of) your rights and seeking your arbitration to Our Lord. Verily, our sins
have broken our backs, and we have withered from the burden of our evils. You are
indeed The Intercessor, whose intercession is readily accepted and to whom the greatest
intercession and the ranks of Maḥmūd and Wasīlah were promised. Verily Allah  has
said: {And if they had come to you when they wronged themselves and sought
forgiveness from Allah, and the Messenger had also asked forgiveness for them, they
would have found Allah Oft-forgiving, Merciful.} We have come unto you as ones who
have wronged themselves and seeking forgiveness from our sins, so intercede for us to
Your Lord. Request him that He may grant us death on your Sunnah, resurrection in
your company, present us in your pond of al-Kauthar, quench our thirst with your

goblet and free us of all disgrace and regret. (We seek) your intercession O’ Messenger of
Allah. [The above Du‘ā’ should be recited thrice]
{O’ Our Lord! Forgive us, and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and do not place
any resentment in our hearts towards those who have believed. Verily, You are the Most
Kind, Most Merciful.}
Thereafter convey the salām of those who had requested you, saying:

Peace be upon You O’ the Two with whom Rasūlullāh  lied down, his Two
Companions, Ministers, Counsellors, Assistants in Dīn and Overseers to the need of the
Muslims after Him. May Allah  recompense You in the best of forms. We have come
here to seek your arbitration so He may intercede for us, and implore him to accept our
efforts, keep us on his religion and grant us death on it, and resurrect us in his company.
Then he should supplicate for himself, his parents, those who requested his du‘ā’s and
the entire Muslim population.

O’ Allah! Verily you have said – and your speech is true – the following: {And if they
had come to you when they wronged themselves and sought forgiveness from Allah, and
the Messenger had also asked forgiveness for them, they would have found Allah Oft-
forgiving, Merciful.} We have thus come as listeners to your speech, adherers to your
command and seekers of intercession from your Prophet to you. O’ Allah! Forgive us,
our fathers, mothers and brothers who preceded us in faith. Don’t place any resentment
in our hearts towards the believers, for O’ Lord, you are the Most Kind, Most Merciful.
{O’ Lord! Grant us in this world that which is good, and in the hereafter that which is
good, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.}{Exalted is your Lord, Lord of
might, above what they describe. May peace be upon the Messengers, and all praise be to
Allah, the Lord of the Worlds.}
Subsequently, add on whatever you may, and supplicate with what is present in your
mind and what Allah  – out of his grace – grants you the tawfīq̣ to.
Visiting the noble monuments
He will then approach the pillar (which is between the grave and the minbar) of Abū
Lubābah , to which he (i.e. Abū Lubābah ) tied himself until Allah  forgave
him. He will offer as many nafl prayers as he wishes, seeking forgiveness and
supplicating for his needs and wants.
He will then approach the rawḍah and offer ṣalāh there, supplicating for his desires
and engaging in tasbīḥ, tahlīl, thanā’ and istighfār excessively.
Thereafter he should come to the minbar and place his hand upon the bark of the
pomegranate tree which has been blessed due to its contact with the body of
Rasūlullāh . He used to rest his hand there whilst giving a khuṭbah to procure its
blessings. He may offer ṣalāh and supplicate to Allah  there.
Next, he will approach ‘the pillar of the Compassionate One’. This was the pillar under

The Chapter of visiting The Prophet of Allah 
which the trunk of a tree is buried. This tree-trunk – which Rasūlullāh  used to use
as a minbar - cried out to him when he left it and delivered a khuṭbah on a proper
minbar. It did not become silent until Rasūlullāh  embraced it in his arms.
He may then procure blessings from any prophetic remnants and blessed places.
Keeping awake at night
One should persevere to keep awake at night during his stay and partake the fortune of
always staying in the company of Rasūlullāh  and visiting him.
Visiting al-Baq̣ī‘
It is mustaḥab to go to al-Baq̣īԑ and visit its graves, especially the grave of the Leader of
Martyrs, Ḥamzah . Thereafter, he should pay a visit to ‘Abbās, Ḥasan ibn ‘Alī 
and the rest of the family of Rasūlullāh . He should then visit the Leader of the
Believers ‘Uthmān , Ibrāhim – the son of the Prophet  – his wives, his aunt
Ṣafiyyah, the rest of his companions and their followers as well . He should also visit
the matyrs of Uḥud, preferably on a Thursday, and say:

May peace be upon You, in lieu of your patience. What an excellent final abode!
He should then recite āyat al-kursī, Sūrah al-Ikhlāṣ (eleven times) and Sūrah Yāsīn (if

Visiting Masjid Q̣ubā’

O’ the Listener of cries, the Helper to aid-seekers, the Alleviator of the anguished, the
Responder to the oppressed! Send peace upon our Master Muḥammad and his family,
and abate my ache and sorrow just as you abated the ache and sorrow of your
Messenger at this place, O’ the Sympathiser, the Conferrer, the Benefactor of good and
favours, the Ever-granter of bounties, the Most Merciful of merciful ones.)
May Allah  send constant peace and blessings upon our Master Muḥammad , his
family and companions forever. O’ Lord of the Worlds, Āmīn.
